# Base-table population plan: a multilingual, multijurisdictional base without an English pivot

Session `session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review`. **A proposal; it approves nothing and writes no rows** (owner statement
2026-11-06, item 5). Planner: `opus/150/synth`. Every figure carries the label of the command in the appendix that derives
it, with its 2026-11-06 result; **re-run the appendix (`python3 <appendix script>` from the repository root) rather than
trust any figure here** (CLAUDE.md rule 7a). Rulings are cited by their ledger heading in `references/project-standards.md`,
not restated.

## 0. Verdict

The base cannot yet be made free of English bias by adding rows, because three mechanisms put English in the pivot:
`terms.canonical_en` is NOT NULL while OR-17 forbids the model to coin a name, so a concept first met in a non-English source
cannot become a term without an invented English name (it has already happened twice, D8); an alias's provenance is a substring
of a free-text `notes` field, and no route can promote an existing model-generated alias by attesting it (D5, D6); and the
other base vocabularies have no home for a label in any language but English. Fix those three in one small tooling PR, then
populate in this order: the screened item-subject catalogue (fast, English, explicitly a seed), then native-language open passes
over each P1-3 jurisdiction's own instruments, interleaved so every language-jurisdiction pair gets its first full reading before
any gets a second. **The one thing that most reduces the chance of missing a quantity is the open pass, in the instrument's own
language, over the full text of each P1-3 jurisdiction's primary accessibility instrument, run to a derived fixed point** (section C.3).
No scan has done an open pass yet: D14 → 9 scans, 0 open passes, 0 full-reads (2026-11-06).

## A. Diagnosis check

Ranked by what wrong thing reaches the guidebook if left. "Brief" means the base review (`base-review.md`) or the orchestrator's
commission.

| # | Defect | Verdict on the brief | Evidence (appendix label → 2026-11-06 result) | What reaches the book if left |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Parameter list is thin | **Confirmed.** | D1 → 10 active; D2 → 94 terms, 1 declined | Silence on quantities nobody listed: the book misses stairs, handrails, controls and the rest, and nothing says so |
| A2 | English pivot in term origin | **Confirmed, and sharper than stated.** The schema requires an English name (`terms.canonical_en NOT NULL`, `PRAGMA table_info(terms)`); `insert_term` never checks the name against the observed phrase (`grep -n 'def insert_term' scripts/db.py`); OR-17 ("It is not acceptable for the model to generate its own phrases/names/aliases", ledger "Owner rulings 2026-10-29 (third)") forbids the only way to satisfy it. Already violated: two terms minted from Dutch observations carry English names no source used, and their Dutch origin phrases are not aliases at all | D8 → TERM-090 from NL *niveauverschillen*, TERM-092 from NL *tussenbordes*, both with typed English names; D9 → 4 NAMES-NEW terms whose name is not inside the observed phrase | Model-coined English labels presented as concepts; concepts that exist only in a non-English instrument are unrecordable, so the book is structurally limited to what English already names |
| A3 | Alias layer nominal | **Confirmed, with corrections.** The counts reproduce (`python3 scripts/audit/alias_provenance_audit.py`: 2382 aliases; 15 verified, all ID; 1163 model-generated; 880 UNKNOWN; 304 curated EN). Missed: (a) provenance is a substring of `notes`, so the blocking gate passes any row whose free text contains a marker (D5); (b) `add-alias` has never run (D6 → 0) although 45 NAMES-EXISTING adjudications exist (D7); (c) `add-alias` refuses an alias already held in that language (`grep -n 'def add_alias' scripts/db.py`), so a model-generated alias can never be promoted by attesting it; (d) 996 rows are typed `TRANSLATION` (D10), which frames every non-English name as a rendering of the English one, the R11 inversion; (e) two alias jurisdictions are not jurisdictions (D23, reported by `jurisdiction_db_vocabulary`) | D4 → 2133 NULL jurisdiction | Searches run on model guesses presented as vocabulary; "native term" claims the database cannot support |
| A4 | ICF English-only and thin | **Confirmed; the titled rows are worse than stated.** None of the 29 titles came from WHO bytes: 17 cite a skill file deleted on 2026-10-14 (`ls skills/functional-deficit-auditor_SKILL.md` fails; `git log --diff-filter=D -- skills/functional-deficit-auditor_SKILL.md`), 12 cite repository prose (D11). `set-icf-title` refuses to overwrite, so there is no correction route. Chapters e4, e5 and d8 are absent (D12) | D11, D12 | ICF titles from memory laundered through repository files: CLAUDE.md 5(c) on a classification |
| A5 | Identity, need, room, medical labels English-only | **Confirmed, and the documented route does not exist.** `governance/functional-taxonomy.md` ("Naming", `grep -n 'Person-first' governance/functional-taxonomy.md`) defers native-language conventions to `term_aliases`, but `term_aliases.term_id` references `terms` only; identity, need, room and medical codes are not terms | `PRAGMA foreign_key_list(term_aliases)` | Identity-first or person-first conventions of each language community cannot be recorded; any non-English rendering would be a translation of English prose |
| A6 | (missed) The language half of a bucket member cannot be derived for a source | **New.** `evidence_sources.language` is NULL on every row; `lang_detected` mixes case and is NULL on 8 (D13). OR-8 makes a bucket member a jurisdiction-and-language pair, so coverage per pair is not computable. The bucket table itself (T-6b steps 4-5, `workplan/2026-10-23-pipeline-resolution-workplan.md`) is not built | D13; `grep -n 'T-6b' workplan/2026-10-23-pipeline-resolution-workplan.md` | A "covered" pair read only in English (e.g. a Swiss instrument read in one of its languages) |
| A7 | (missed) No open pass, all scans pre-screen | **New.** | D14 → 9 / 0 / 0; `python3 scripts/audit/scan_debt.py` → DEBT 477 pairs | Every quantity outside the 10 is unread in every held source |
| A8 | (missed) Prose callers contradict the database | **New.** `references/native-alias-verification.md` and `references/methodology-native-alias-verification.md` carry hand-typed counts, call search-time acceptance "CLEAN … verified", and use "P1/P2" for language priority, which collides with the P1-3 jurisdiction scope. `skills/multilingual-research_SKILL.md` hard-codes 19 languages × 46 jurisdictions with numeric floors and "Synthesises findings in English" (`grep -n '46 jurisdictions' skills/multilingual-research_SKILL.md`), against OR-12a and the P1-3 scope. `scripts/generate_alias_chart.py`, named in the commission, does not exist | the greps shown | A session follows the prose, not the database (CLAUDE.md 5(b)) |
| A9 | Mixed kinds in `terms` | **Confirmed.** Lens terms (17 `functional_axis`), methods (14), medical (8), economics, legal and population terms sit beside quantities (D18). The 2026-10-09 seed ruling made "the terms registry" the seed; read literally, every row is a parameter candidate | D18 | Elements and lens terms minted as parameters, or the scan contract measured against terms that can never hold a value, inflating scan debt |
| A10 | Medical lens empty | **Confirmed, with two corrections.** `medical_lens_integrity` is **advisory**, not blocking (`python3 scripts/run_checks.py --list \| grep medical`). The binding ruling is the ledger entry "CORRECTION, same day — 'demand-populated' re-instated a position the owner had overruled" (2026-09-11): populate by correspondence from the identity registry and functional axes first, at block grain, then on demand. The empty table is an unexecuted ruling, not a deferral | D21 → 0/0/0; both crossing maps appear in the UNWRITABLE set (CLAUDE.md section 4 script) until a medical row exists; `add-medical` writes row and crossing together, so this is not a trap | A reader arriving with a diagnosis has no route in |
| A11 | Rooms uncategorised | **Confirmed, and rooms have no reader.** No foreign key points at `rooms` and no script queries it (D19; `git grep -n 'FROM rooms\|JOIN rooms' -- scripts ':!scripts/migrations'` → nothing). Two rows read as near-duplicates (circulation corridor versus hallway) | D19 | Low: nothing renders it. Populating it before a reader exists is apparatus (CLAUDE.md section 8) |
| A12 | (missed) Stakes unassigned and vocabulary held twice | **New.** 16 of 17 needs lack `typical_stakes` (D20); `access_stakes` is a table holding the same three values as the CHECK on `access_needs.typical_stakes`, with no foreign key (rule 8) | D20; `PRAGMA foreign_key_list(access_needs)` | Low until determinations weigh stakes |
| A13 | Direction coverage | **Confirmed.** | D3 → 2 of 10 | The most-accommodating rule (OR-4) cannot pick for 8 parameters |
| A14 | (missed) Language varieties and in-scope official languages | **New, partly DG-NON.** `lang_jur_map` uses one code for Norwegian (no Bokmål/Nynorsk split) and one for Chinese (no script); AT is mapped but not in `schemas/enums.py`; official languages of P1-3 jurisdictions outside the 14 are absent. D15 → 39 P1-3 pairs over 14 languages | D15; `python3 scripts/audit/jurisdiction_db_vocabulary.py` | Two written standards of one language conflated; jurisdictions whose instrument exists in a language the map lacks are read in none |
| A15 | (missed) Three P1-3 jurisdictions have nothing to read | **New.** No code lead and no held instrument for DK, IT, CN (D16) | D16 | Their quantities can only arrive through other jurisdictions' framing |
| A16 | Slug topic gaps | **Confirmed, low.** The 2026-10-09 scan contract makes slugs plan searches only; they do not bound vocabulary | base review table, `slugs` row | Only search planning |
| A17 | (missed) Stage assignment: an alias copies an evidence-stage fact | **New.** A source-attested alias stores the observation's surface form and points back only in prose (`notes`). Under CLAUDE.md section 3 the phrase belongs to evidence (`observed_terms`); the base row should point, not copy (rule 5) | `PRAGMA table_info(term_aliases)` | The alias and its observation drift apart, and only the alias is read |

**The canonical_en question, answered.** True as stated, and OR-17 turns it from a bias into a contradiction: the schema
demands an English string for every concept, and the rulings forbid the model to supply one that no source used. What follows is
design question B.1. A rename or drop is ruled out: six committed data migrations name the column
(`grep -l canonical_en scripts/migrations/data_*`) and two INSERT into `terms` (`grep -l 'INSERT INTO "terms"' scripts/migrations/*`),
so the column can never be dropped (rule 5), and readers are numerous
(`grep -c canonical_en scripts/db.py`; `grep -rln canonical_en scripts --include=*.py`).

**One correction to the 2026-11-06 ledger entry.** Its item 3 says admitting the item subjects is "a schema change plus a
resolver". No schema change is needed: `terms.catalogue`'s CHECK already admits `_archived/data/corpus-pre-reset-2026-08-06.db`
(`PRAGMA table_info(terms)` / `select sql from sqlite_master where name='terms'`); only `_resolve_catalogue_entry` refuses
anything but `terms:<TERM-ID>`. The session should record that correction in the ledger (rule 0's record-keeping; no owner
decision needed).

## B. Population design, per table

Principles applied to every row of the table below:

- **No row in language X is derived from a row in English.** Every non-English label or alias points at an in-language
  artefact (an observation whose quote verifies in a saved file, or a persisted payload). English is one language among 14
  and gets the same pointer requirement for its jurisdiction variants.
- **Language and jurisdiction are read, not typed** (rule 8): from the observation and its source, as `add-alias` already does.
- **No language CHECK is added.** The language vocabulary is `lang_jur_map`, so a language admitted later is a row, not a migration.

| Table | Target end-state | Single source of truth | Derived, not curated | Pointer | Writer (existing verb, or gap) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `terms` | Every concept any P1-3 instrument treats as a design quantity, element, method or setting, each with provenance: an origin observation (NAMES-NEW) or an approved catalogue entry | the origin observation, or the catalogue entry plus approval heading | The label's language: from the origin observation; `en` for a catalogue mint | `term_adjudications` → `observed_terms` → `evidence_sources` | `add-term --from-observation`; `mint-term-from-catalogue`. **Gap T2:** bind the name to the observed phrase |
| `base_parameters` | Every term that names a quantity under determination; every other term declined with a reason | `terms` + the promotion or declination | Nothing curated; status from verbs | `term_id` (UNIQUE) | `add-parameter`, `decline-parameter`, `merge-parameter`, `set-parameter-direction` |
| `term_aliases` | For each term and each P1-3 pair: the phrase that jurisdiction's own instrument uses, attested; model-generated rows held as flagged search aids only | `observed_terms` row (phrase, language, locator, quote) | alias text, language, jurisdiction: read from the observation and source | **Gap T3:** a nullable `observation_id` foreign key | `add-alias`; **gap T3:** attach a pointer to an already-held alias instead of refusing |
| `base_icf` | Every code a held need, identity or parameter crosses to, plus chapters d4, d5, e1, e2, e3, e4, e5 as a completeness frame; English title from WHO bytes | persisted WHO payload | title verified as a substring of the payload | `title_source = payload:<file>` | `add-icf-code`, `set-icf-title --title-payload`; **gap T4:** replace a non-payload title with a payload-verified one, recording the old |
| Labels in other languages (ICF titles, identity, need, room, medical display names) | One label per code per language (and per jurisdiction where usage differs), each pointing at its in-language artefact | the artefact | language, jurisdiction from the artefact | **Proposed T5:** one table, five nullable foreign keys (identity, need, ICF, medical, room), CHECK exactly one, mirroring the ruled four-lens-column shape (ledger, 2026-08-28 lens ruling as amended by D-0182) | none today; T5 waits on owner decisions E5, E6, E8 |
| `base_taxonomy_identity` | Unchanged (DG-NON). Labels per language through T5 | owner rulings | — | — | none, deliberately |
| `access_needs` / `access_need_icf` | Stakes assigned with warrant; ICF crossings `confirmed` only against WHO bytes | owner-approved table for stakes | stakes vocabulary from the column CHECK; retire `access_stakes` if nothing reads it (§8) | `access_need_icf` | **[GAP]** no verb found for `typical_stakes`; confirm with `grep -n 'typical_stakes' scripts/db.py` before planning one |
| `base_taxonomy_medical` + maps | The correspondence set the 2026-09-11 correction bounds, then on demand | WHO ICD-11 release file, persisted | anchors verified from bytes (`icd11_verified_at`) | crossings to identity and ICF | `add-medical --icd11-payload` |
| `rooms` | Frozen until a reader exists (E8) | — | — | none points at it | none needed |
| `lang_jur_map` | The 39 P1-3 pairs (D15) approved as bucket members; varieties per E7 | owner approval per row (T-6b) | — | bucket table points at pairs (OR-8) | T-6b, already ruled; not new here |

### B.1 How a concept that originates in a non-English source becomes a term

| Option | What it does | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A (recommended).** The term's label is the source's own phrase, in its own language; `canonical_en` holds it verbatim; the label's language is derived from the NAMES-NEW observation | No schema change. `add-term` gains one refusal: the name must occur, case-folded, in the observation's `surface_form` (T2). An English name is added only when an English-language instrument of a P1-3 jurisdiction is observed naming the same concept; then `rename-term --from-observation` | Satisfies OR-17 and R11 at once; English loses its privilege; the reader sees the concept as the instrument names it | The column name lies; every reader that renders `canonical_en` must show the label's language. `rename-term` turns the old name into a DEPRECATED alias, which is wrong for a native label: T2 must make it a live SYNONYM in its own language instead |
| B. Rebuild `terms` with `canonical_en` nullable, plus a derived per-language label view | Honest column semantics | Clean model | A table rebuild against every reader (`grep -c canonical_en scripts/db.py`) and the views that name it; net code grows; no ruling needs it yet |
| C. A typed English gloss | — | — | Forbidden by OR-17; listed only to reject |

The definition and scope note may describe the concept in English prose, because prose is ours (the 2026-09-11 reasoning,
"identifiers are facts while prose is ours"); a name may not be invented. Remediation of D8 and D9: flag the four terms now; correct
each in a data PR by `rename-term` to the observed phrase, on the owner's word for the parameter among them (TERM-091 is parameter 12).

### B.2 Native term versus translation

- **Rule.** An attested alias is a phrase a jurisdiction's own instrument uses, observed in that instrument in its own language.
  It is typed SYNONYM, NARROWER or BROADER, never TRANSLATION (T3 refuses TRANSLATION on an attested alias). An officially
  published English version of a non-English instrument is a translation: its phrases are observed with the language they appear
  in, but they attest the English-language usage of nobody's jurisdiction and are excluded from `add-alias` for an EN alias unless
  the instrument is authoritative in English in that jurisdiction (T3 refuses where the alias language is not paired with the
  source's jurisdiction in `lang_jur_map`).
- **Jurisdiction tagging** is the source's jurisdiction, read by `add-alias`. That already separates DE/AT/CH German, FR/BE/CH/CA
  French, NL/BE Dutch, PT usage, and US/UK/AU/CA/IE/NZ/SG English. It does not separate two written standards inside one
  jurisdiction (Norwegian Bokmål and Nynorsk) or scripts (Chinese), which is E7.
- **Legal designations** (a JA, KO or ZH statutory term of art) are terms in their own right under B.1, not aliases of an English
  concept, wherever the instrument defines them.

### B.3 Verifying the 880 unrecorded and 1163 model-generated aliases

Status meanwhile: **usable only as flagged search aids** (OR-12b), **never vocabulary** (OR-17), pending the owner's OR-17b (E4).
The route is not a separate glossary-verification protocol but the ordinary evidence path, which removes the need for
`VERIFIED-GLOSSARY` as a hand marker (rule 8):

1. Per language, the glossary is the P1-3 instrument's own definitions clause, or a national standards body's terminology
   standard, admitted as a source (`add-source`), its text persisted with `scripts/research/retrieval_log.py` `fetch()` and
   registered with `scripts/research/full_text.py`. Wayback `if_` fallback per CLAUDE.md section 7 for a block.
2. Each phrase found is `observe-term`'d with locator and verbatim quote, `adjudicate-term`'d NAMES-EXISTING, then `add-alias`.
   With T3, a held model-generated alias whose text matches gains the pointer in place and becomes attested; an attested phrase
   not held becomes a new row.
3. A model-generated alias the instrument contradicts, or never uses after a full open pass of that pair, stays flagged; whether it
   is deleted is E4. No alias is ever generated to fill a gap (OR-17).

Order: one language at a time, the instrument with the largest definitions section first. `alias_provenance_audit` reports
progress per language; it must classify from the pointer (T3), or it measures text, not attestation.

### B.4 ICF and ICD-11 titles in each language

- **English titles first**, from a WHO ICF payload persisted under `retrieval-log/`, through `set-icf-title --title-payload`; T4
  replaces the 29 non-payload titles. Before T4 ships, confirm the payload check anchors the title to its code, not just anywhere in
  the file ([GAP]: `set_icf_title` tests `title in body`, a substring match a neighbouring code's title can satisfy).
- **Other languages** go to the T5 label table, each label pointing at a persisted WHO or national-body payload in that language.
  Which of the 14 languages WHO or national bodies publish for ICF and for ICD-11 is **[UNVERIFIED]**; measure by retrieval, never
  by recollection. The ICD-11 English release file is already held (`ls retrieval-log/session_2026-09-11-medical-lens-icd11`).
- **Is a translation table a second home?** No, if it holds only non-derivable facts: WHO's published title in language X is a
  different fact from its English title, keyed on the same code (a pointer, rule 5). It becomes a second home if it also holds the
  English title already in `base_icf.title`; T5 therefore refuses an English row for a code that `base_icf` titles. Whether the
  titles may be stored verbatim under the guidebook's licence is E5 (DG-NON, licensing).

### B.5 Identity, access-need, room and stakes labels

- Identity codes and English display names are untouched (DG-NON). A label in language X is the community's own designation,
  attested in an in-language Co-1 source of a P1-3 jurisdiction, never a translation of the English display name. Where communities
  in one language differ (identity-first versus person-first), the label carries its jurisdiction; where no attestation exists the
  code has no label in X and the gap is visible. Mechanism and certifier are E6.
- Need labels and medical display names are our prose; a non-English rendering is a translation of our prose, which R11 does not
  forbid for prose but must be marked as ours. Defer until a reader in that language exists (no render work is in scope).
- Rooms: frozen (E8). Stakes: one owner-approved table (E9).

### B.6 The medical lens

Populate, in this order: (1) the correspondence set under the 2026-09-11 CORRECTION entry, from the identity registry and the
functional-axis terms, excluding the identity-first and umbrella codes that entry and `governance/functional-taxonomy.md` name;
anchor on the block whose title states the presentation; every anchor verified against the persisted release file through
`add-medical --icd11-payload`; (2) then on demand from admitted sources. Leave empty: entity-level codes, any chapter mirror, and
any row whose anchor cannot be verified from bytes (`icd11_verified_at` stays NULL and the row is not written). Medical display
names are our prose (the `insert_medical` docstring). This is Opus-class judgment (pruning the derived join, per the 2026-09-11
ruling) and its own research PR.

## C. Route to a comprehensive parameter list

### C.1 The screened catalogue of item subjects (route i)

A read-only subcommand (T1) prints one table for the owner. It never writes the database. Per row:

| Column | Filled by | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| pointer | machine | `items:<rowid>` into the pre-reset database; the old code is not shown (the 2026-11-06 ruling: "with their codes removed") |
| stripped name | machine | parentheticals and bracketed text removed; then `_VALUE_BEARING` and `_ITEM_CODE` re-tested (imported, not retyped) |
| still value-bearing | machine | D22 → 2 of 93 after stripping (2026-11-06) |
| prescription-bearing | judgment | condition clauses the regex cannot see (DR-2026-08-19 section 1.1 counted names carrying prescriptive conditions); a yes means reject or reword from a source, never mint |
| nearest held term | machine | `_name_holder` on name and aliases; D22 → 8 exact matches |
| kind | judgment, from `quantity / element / intervention / method / setting / lens` | |
| quantity implied | judgment | **a lead only.** The implied quantity's name is not in the item name, so minting it would be coining; it goes to the open-pass lead list |
| recommendation and reason | judgment | mint as term and promote (quantity); mint as term and decline (element, intervention: `decline-parameter --reason`); hold as lead; reject (held, prescription-bearing, or not ours) |

The owner approves the table in a dated ledger entry; then `mint-term-from-catalogue --catalogue _archived/data/corpus-pre-reset-2026-08-06.db
--entry-ref items:<rowid> --approval-ref "<heading>"` per approved row, followed by `add-parameter` or `decline-parameter`.
An element is a term, never a parameter (OR-14: element pages derive from parameters through a typed pointer). The catalogue
seeds English names only; it decides nothing about whether a concept exists, and every term it mints enters the alias coverage
metric with zero attested pairs.

### C.2 The open pass over held codes (route ii, OR-13 and OR-16)

Held texts are derived, not listed: for each instrument, `grep -l '"<ref_id>"' retrieval-log/*/manifest.jsonl` and
`select * from v_scan_ledger where ref_id = ?`. Most held non-English codes are single clauses retrieved for the ramp work (titles
naming one section, e.g. `select ref_id, original_title from evidence_sources where evidence_type='code'`). So route ii gives
full texts mainly for SG, UK, US and IE; it is the fastest first step and the most English one, which is why C.3 interleaves.
Each reading: `record-scan --mode catalogue --method full-read --text-scope full --open-pass-done`, with every new design quantity
`observe-term`'d verbatim.

### C.3 Native-language open passes over P1-3 instruments (route iii)

1. **Instrument list per pair**, derived from `research_code_leads`, `references/standards-registry.md` and the held codes,
   restricted to current editions (HANDOFF section 3). DK, IT and CN have nothing (D16): their first act is a search for the primary
   instrument, logged per R8.
2. **Order:** one full open pass per pair before any pair's second; within that, free official full texts before paywalled ones
   (availability per instrument is [UNVERIFIED] until fetched); English pairs are not first. A block goes to the Wayback route of
   CLAUDE.md section 7, with its recorded limit (the CSA B651 failure).
3. **Stopping rule, derived.** A pair is exhausted when every current instrument on its list has a full-read, full-scope, open-pass
   scan at the current `catalogue_version`, and the last such round produced no NAMES-NEW and no DEFERRED observation for that pair.
   A new parameter raises the catalogue version and `scan_debt` re-opens targeted readings, so the list closes only at a fixed point
   where a whole round adds nothing. No count is set by hand.

### C.4 Completeness checks from the other direction (route iv)

ICF chapters d4, d5, d6, d9 and e1 to e5 (from the WHO payload), `research_code_leads`, and the standards registries are read as
**checks**, not name sources: for each ICF activity or environmental code, ask whether any parameter's term addresses it; a miss is a
lead for the open pass, recorded as a gap. No ruling permits naming a parameter from ICF text.

### C.5 Coverage metric (OR-8), computed from the database

For each active parameter *p* and each approved bucket member (*L*, *J*):

- **read(p, L, J)**: some current instrument of *J* whose text language is *L* has a `v_scan_ledger` status of EXTRACTED,
  STATED-ABSENT or READ-NOTHING-FOUND for *p*. Needs A6 fixed (source language populated) and T-6b built.
- **named(p, L, J)**: an attested alias (pointer, T3) of *p*'s term in *L* from a source of *J*.

Report both per parameter and per pair, as counts with the command, never as a stored figure. It ships as one view in the T-6b PR,
which already plans `v_coverage_parameter_via_admission`; extend that rather than add a second view.

### C.6 Priority order

1. T1-T4 tooling PR. 2. Screened catalogue table, owner approval, mints and declinations. 3. Decline the non-quantity terms
already held (lens, method, economics and similar, D18) with reasons. 4. Route ii open passes. 5. Route iii, interleaved.
6. Alias attestation (B.3) rides on 4 and 5; nothing is attested separately from a reading. 7. ICF English titles, then labels.
8. Medical correspondence set. 9. Directions (`set-parameter-direction`) for each parameter as it is promoted.

## D. Sequencing and pull requests

Rule 10 splits tooling from rows; rule 9: each PR opened once, last, unsubscribed immediately, never watched. The gate for every PR
is CLAUDE.md section 1: `scripts/preflight.sh`, then `python3 scripts/run_checks.py --changed-from origin/main --explain`, plus
`--selftest` if anything is renamed. The checks below are the ones that read what each PR changes
(`python3 scripts/run_checks.py --list`); for each, the question is whether it could go red on that PR's defect.

| PR | Content | Depends on | Checks that read it | Adversarial pass |
|---|---|---|---|---|

content.text:
The Opus plan is written and pushed to PR #213. It is a proposal only: it writes no rows and approves nothing. The plan is `scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/base-population-plan.md`. I re-ran four of its figures and they reproduce; the rest I did not re-derive.

**Verdict.** Adding rows alone will not remove the English bias. Three mechanisms put English at the centre:
1. **Term names.** `terms.canonical_en` is required, but your OR-17 forbids the model to coin names. Two terms already break this: TERM-090 and TERM-092 came from Dutch phrases but carry English names no source used.
2. **Alias provenance.** It is free text in a notes field. A model-generated alias already held can never be upgraded by attesting it, and `add-alias` has never been run.
3. **Other labels.** Identity, access-need, room and ICF labels have nowhere to hold a non-English form.

**Corrections to my review.**
- None of the 29 ICF titles came from WHO text. 17 cite a skill file deleted on 2026-10-14, and 12 cite repository prose.
- The medical-lens check is advisory, not blocking.
- Rooms have no reader.
- Source language is NULL on all 58 sources, so coverage per language and jurisdiction cannot be computed yet.
- I also wrongly told you a schema change was needed to admit the item subjects. Only a resolver is needed; I corrected the ledger entry.

**The plan's order.**
1. A tooling-only PR:
   - the item-subject resolver and a read-only screen table;
   - a refusal when a term's name isn't in the phrase it came from;
   - a pointer from each alias to the observation behind it;
   - a route to replace non-WHO ICF titles.
2. The screened table of the 93 item subjects goes to you for approval. Elements are minted as terms and then declined as parameters.
3. Open passes over the codes we hold, then in each jurisdiction's own language. These are interleaved so every language-and-jurisdiction pair is read once before any is read twice. They stop at a derived point where a full round adds nothing new.

The open pass in each instrument's own language is the biggest protection against missing a quantity, and none has been done yet.

**Decisions that block the first PR** (each is written as a phone-sized prompt in the plan, section E):
1. **E1:** how a concept first met outside English is named. Recommended: the code's own phrase, in its own language, until an English-language code naming the same thing is found. Only you can decide this.
2. **E3:** point at the item subjects by row number, so no old codes appear in live rows. Recommended: yes.
3. **E4 (OR-17b):** the 2,043 unattested aliases stay as flagged search aids, not vocabulary, and are not deleted. Recommended: yes.

Nine further decisions can wait. Some are licensing, identity names in other languages, and language varieties such as Norwegian Bokmål and Nynorsk or Chinese scripts. Arabic, Bengali, Hindi and Swahili remain scoped out under OR-12a. The plan says the design could admit them later without a schema change.

**What the plan could not verify.**
- Which of the 14 languages WHO publishes ICF and ICD-11 in, and under what licence.
- Which P1-3 instruments are free in full text.
- Whether Denmark, Italy and China have any instrument held at all.

The plan treats those as unverified, to be measured by retrieval.

I did not run the diff-scoped gate. The diff is scratchpad files plus one ledger entry, and PR #213 stays unwatched per rule 9. The two always-growing logs (`commands.jsonl` and `transcripts/`) are left uncommitted, as CLAUDE.md §7 says.

def insert_term(from_observation: int, canonical_en: str, rationale: str, session: str,
                definition: str = None, domain: str = None, scope_note: str = None,
                dry_run: bool = False):
    """Mint a term for a concept new to the vocabulary, AND adjudicate it in one act.

    The missing half of D-0173. `adjudicate-term --outcome NAMES-NEW` refuses unless the
    term already exists -- "create the term first, then adjudicate NAMES-NEW to it" --
    and nothing created one, so NAMES-NEW was an outcome the CLI documented and could
    not reach. A checker whose satisfying writer does not exist is a trap (CLAUDE.md §8).

    Term and adjudication land together because they are one judgement: *this observed
    phrase names a concept we did not hold, and here is the term for it.* Splitting them
    would permit a term with no provenance, which is the contamination the owner objected
    to on 2026-09-09 -- prior-version containers that exist before the work does.
    """
    canonical_en = (canonical_en or "").strip()
    rationale = (rationale or "").strip()
    if not canonical_en:
        raise Refusal("--canonical-en is required: a term is its name.")
    if not rationale:
        raise Refusal(
            "--rationale is required. Minting a term is an adjudication, and an "
            "adjudication that does not say why cannot be contested.")
    if _VALUE_BEARING.search(canonical_en):
        raise Refusal(
            f"--canonical-en {canonical_en!r} REFUSED: it carries a number, a comparator "
            f"or a min/max word, so it states a determination in its own name.\n"
            f"That is the defect the item layer was deleted for -- a container that "
            f"announces its answer predisposes every finding filed into it "
            f"(DR-2026-08-19 §1.1: 42 of 93 item names embedded a determination).\n"
            f"Name the PARAMETER, not the value: 'corridor width', not "
            f"'corridor width >=1200 mm'. The value belongs in the determination.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        obs = conn.execute("SELECT observation_id, surface_form, ref_id FROM observed_terms "
                           "WHERE observation_id=?", [from_observation]).fetchone()
        if obs is None:
            raise Refusal(
                f"observation {from_observation}: no such observed term. A term is minted "
                f"FROM an observed phrase (db.py observe-term), never from nothing -- that "
                f"is what makes the vocabulary an output of the work rather than a "
                f"presupposition.")
        clash = _name_holder(conn, canonical_en, aliases=False)
        if clash:
            raise Refusal(
                f"{canonical_en!r} is already TERM {clash['term_id']} "
                f"({clash['detail']!r}). That makes this NAMES-EXISTING, not "
                f"NAMES-NEW:\n  db.py adjudicate-term --observation-id {from_observation} "
                f"--outcome NAMES-EXISTING --term-id {clash['term_id']} --rationale ...")
        term_id = _mint_term_id(conn)
        row = {"term_id": term_id, "canonical_en": canonical_en,
               "definition": definition, "domain": domain, "scope_note": scope_note}
        row.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "terms", session))
        conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO terms ({','.join(row)}) "
                     f"VALUES ({','.join('?'*len(row))})", list(row.values()))
        adj = {"observation_id": from_observation, "outcome": "NAMES-NEW",
               "term_id": term_id, "rationale": rationale}
        adj.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "term_adjudications", session))
        cur = conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO term_adjudications ({','.join(adj)}) "
                           f"VALUES ({','.join('?'*len(adj))})", list(adj.values()))
        return {"term_id": term_id, "canonical_en": canonical_en,
                "adjudication_id": cur.lastrowid, "from_surface_form": obs["surface_form"],
                "from_ref_id": obs["ref_id"], "dry_run": dry_run}


def _mint_term_id(conn) -> str:
    """The next TERM-NNN. Computed, never stored -- a counter table would be a second
    home for a fact the column already states (rule 5). Same discipline as
    dbcore.next_ref_id. One home since 2026-10-09: add-term and mint-term-from-catalogue
    both mint, and two copies of this arithmetic could disagree on the next id."""
    top = conn.execute("SELECT max(CAST(substr(term_id,6) AS INTEGER)) FROM terms "
                       "WHERE term_id LIKE 'TERM-___'").fetchone()[0] or 0
    return f"TERM-{top + 1:03d}"

def add_alias(term_id: str, observation_id: int, alias_type: str, session: str,
              dry_run: bool = False):
    """Record a SOURCE-ATTESTED alias: a phrase an admitted source uses for this term.

    `term_aliases` had no writer at all (critique F5, missed by the critic: only the 057
    baseline and a selftest inserted into it), so a new language alias had no sanctioned
    path. Existing aliases are model-generated, curated, or predate provenance marking
    (alias_provenance_audit counts each class); aliases are a reading aid, never evidence
    (catalogue-plan-v2 section 3.9), and this is the route by which source-attested ones
    grow.

    NOTHING IS TYPED THAT THE MACHINE CAN READ (CLAUDE.md rule 8): the alias IS the
    observation's surface form, its language is the observation's (in term_aliases' own
    letter case, measured by _alias_language), and its jurisdiction is the source's. The
    operator chooses only the alias type, from the column's CHECK.

    REFUSES: an alias type outside the CHECK, or DEPRECATED (rename-term's record); an
    unknown term or observation; an observation no adjudication names this term with; an
    observation whose phrase is not inside its quote, or whose quote is not in a file saved
    for its source (unless the observation carries a recorded VERBATIM-EXEMPT); an alias
    the term already holds in that language. The notes carry `source-attested`, the
    provenance marker alias_provenance_audit reads, with the observation and source.
    """
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        dbcore.check_declared(conn, "term_aliases", "alias_type", alias_type,
                              "add-alias --alias-type")
        if alias_type == "DEPRECATED":
            raise Refusal("add-alias: DEPRECATED marks a former canonical name, which only "
                          "rename-term records. A phrase a source uses is a live alias.")
        if not dbcore.exists(conn, "terms", "term_id", term_id):
            raise Refusal(f"add-alias: {term_id!r}: no such term.")
        obs = conn.execute(
            "SELECT o.observation_id, o.ref_id, o.surface_form, o.language, o.locator, "
            "o.context_quote, o.notes, e.jurisdiction FROM observed_terms o "
            "JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = o.ref_id WHERE o.observation_id = ?",
            (observation_id,)).fetchone()
        if obs is None:
            raise Refusal(f"add-alias: observation {observation_id}: no such observed term.")
        if not _names_term(conn, observation_id, term_id):
            raise Refusal(
                f"add-alias: no adjudication of observation {observation_id} names "
                f"{term_id}. An alias says the source's phrase names THIS concept, which is "
                f"a judgement: db.py adjudicate-term --observation-id {observation_id} "
                f"--outcome NAMES-EXISTING --term-id {term_id} --rationale ... first.")
        quote = obs["context_quote"] or ""
        kind, where, inside = _retrieval_log().classify_observation(
            obs["surface_form"], quote, obs["notes"], obs["ref_id"])
        if not quote.strip() or not inside:
            raise Refusal(
                f"add-alias: observation {observation_id} carries no context quote that "
                f"contains its phrase, so nothing attests the phrase was seen. Observe the "
                f"sighting again with --locator and --context-quote (db.py observe-term), "
                f"adjudicate it, and alias from that observation.")
        if kind not in ("scoped", "exempt"):
            raise Refusal(
                f"add-alias: observation {observation_id}'s quote is not in a file saved for "
                f"{obs['ref_id']} ({where}), so 'source-attested' would be untrue. Register "
                f"the source's text (scripts/research/full_text.py) and observe the sighting "
                f"from it, or record why no artefact can carry it (observe-term "
                f"--verbatim-exempt). Nothing was written.")
        lang = _alias_language(conn, obs["language"] or "EN")
        held = conn.execute("SELECT alias_type FROM term_aliases WHERE term_id = ? "
                            "AND alias = ? AND language = ?",
                            (term_id, obs["surface_form"], lang)).fetchone()
        if held:
            raise Refusal(f"add-alias: {term_id} already holds {obs['surface_form']!r} "
                          f"({lang}) as {held[0]}. Nothing was written.")
        others = [r[0] for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT DISTINCT term_id FROM term_aliases WHERE alias = ? AND language = ? "
            "AND term_id <> ?", (obs["surface_form"], lang, term_id))]
        note = (f"source-attested: observation {observation_id}, {obs['ref_id']} at "
                f"{obs['locator']!r}; " + (f"quote verified in {where.split(',')[0]}"
                                          if kind == "scoped" else
                                          "the observation's quote is VERBATIM-EXEMPT"))
        row = {"term_id": term_id, "alias": obs["surface_form"], "language": lang,
               "alias_type": alias_type, "jurisdiction": obs["jurisdiction"],
               "notes": note}
        row.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "term_aliases", session))
        conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO term_aliases ({','.join(row)}) "
                     f"VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(row))})", list(row.values()))
        return {"term_id": term_id, "alias": obs["surface_form"], "language": lang,
                "alias_type": alias_type, "jurisdiction": obs["jurisdiction"],
                "also_an_alias_of": others, "dry_run": dry_run}


def _decision_reference(ref: str) -> str:
    """A decision reference that resolves, or a Refusal naming the two accepted forms.

    Either a decision record under decisions/ that exists, or an owner ruling quoted
    exactly once in the ledger, written `references/project-standards.md :: "<quote>"`
    (the form dispose-adversarial-finding's OWNER-RULED disposition reads).
    """
    ref = (ref or "").strip()
    m = dbcore.LEDGER_REF_RE.match(ref)
    if m:
        dbcore.require_ledger_quote_once(m.group(1), "--decision-ref: the quote")
        return ref
    path = dbcore.resolve_under(dbcore.REPO_ROOT / "decisions", ref) if ref else None
    if path is not None and path.is_file():
        return ref
    raise Refusal(
        "--decision-ref must name the decision that reverses the declination: a decision "
        "record that exists under decisions/ (decisions/DR-....md), or an owner ruling as "
        "'references/project-standards.md :: \"<verbatim quote>\"', found once. Reversing "
        "a declination is a recorded decision (governance/decision-protocol.md), not an "
        f"edit. Got {ref!r}.")


def revoke_declination(term_id: str, reason: str, decision_ref: str, session: str,
                       dry_run: bool = False):
    """Revoke a declination: the term may be promoted after all. The row stays.

    Migration 101 shipped no un-decline verb, "nothing reads an un-decline yet". The
    reader now exists: the cohort's vocabulary review (catalogue-plan-v2 section 3.4),
    which may find a declined term is a quantity after all. Retire in place (owner
    2026-09-16): revoked_at / revoked_by_session / revocation_reason are set (migration
    104) and every reader treats a revoked declination as absent -- add-parameter's
    declined-term refusal, research_batch_dod R16's 'disposed', the adversarial skill's
    declination query.

    REFUSES: a blank reason; a decision reference that does not resolve
    (_decision_reference); a term with no declination; one already revoked.
    KNOWN LIMIT, stated: one declination row per term (the PRIMARY KEY), so a revoked
    declination cannot be followed by a second one; decline-parameter says so.
    """
    reason = dbcore.require_reason(
        reason, term_id, why="A revocation that cannot say why cannot be contested.")
    ref = _decision_reference(decision_ref)
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        row = conn.execute("SELECT reason, created_by_session, revoked_at, "
                           "revoked_by_session FROM parameter_declinations "
                           "WHERE term_id = ?", (term_id,)).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise Refusal(f"revoke-declination: {term_id} is not declined. Nothing was "
                          f"written.")
        if row["revoked_at"]:
            raise Refusal(f"revoke-declination: {term_id}'s declination was already "
                          f"revoked by {row['revoked_by_session']} at {row['revoked_at']}. "
                          f"Nothing was written.")
        stamp = dbcore.now()
        conn.execute("UPDATE parameter_declinations SET revoked_at = ?, "
                     "revoked_by_session = ?, revocation_reason = ? WHERE term_id = ?",
                     (stamp, session, f"{reason} (decision: {ref})", term_id))
        return {"term_id": term_id, "revoked": True, "declination_was": row["reason"],

            "JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = o.ref_id WHERE o.observation_id = ?",

        if obs is None:

        if not _names_term(conn, observation_id, term_id):
            raise Refusal(
                f"add-alias: no adjudication of observation {observation_id} names "
                f"{term_id}. An alias says the source's phrase names THIS concept, which is "
                f"a judgement: db.py adjudicate-term --observation-id {observation_id} "
                f"--outcome NAMES-EXISTING --term-id {term_id} --rationale ... first.")
        quote = obs["context_quote"] or ""
        kind, where, inside = _retrieval_log().classify_observation(
            obs["surface_form"], quote, obs["notes"], obs["ref_id"])
        if not quote.strip() or not inside:
            raise Refusal(
                f"add-alias: observation {observation_id} carries no context quote that "
                f"contains its phrase, so nothing attests the phrase was seen. Observe the "
                f"sighting again with --locator and --context-quote (db.py observe-term), "
                f"adjudicate it, and alias from that observation.")
        if kind not in ("scoped", "exempt"):

                f"add-alias: observation {observation_id}'s quote is not in a file saved for "
                f"{obs['ref_id']} ({where}), so 'source-attested' would be untrue. Register "
                f"the source's text (scripts/research/full_text.py) and observe the sighting "
                f"from it, or record why no artefact can carry it (observe-term "
                f"--verbatim-exempt). Nothing was written.")
        lang = _alias_language(conn, obs["language"] or "EN")
        held = conn.execute("SELECT alias_type FROM term_aliases WHERE term_id = ? "
                            "AND alias = ? AND language = ?",
                            (term_id, obs["surface_form"], lang)).fetchone()
        if held:
            raise Refusal(f"add-alias: {term_id} already holds {obs['surface_form']!r} "
                          f"({lang}) as {held[0]}. Nothing was written.")
        others = [r[0] for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT DISTINCT term_id FROM term_aliases WHERE alias = ? AND language = ? "
            "AND term_id <> ?", (obs["surface_form"], lang, term_id))]
        note = (f"source-attested: observation {observation_id}, {obs['ref_id']} at "
                f"{obs['locator']!r}; " + (f"quote verified in {where.split(',')[0]}"
                                          if kind == "scoped" else
                                          "the observation's quote is VERBATIM-EXEMPT"))
        row = {"term_id": term_id, "alias": obs["surface_form"], "language": lang,
               "alias_type": alias_type, "jurisdiction": obs["jurisdiction"],
               "notes": note}
        row.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "term_aliases", session))
        conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO term_aliases ({','.join(row)}) "
                     f"VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(row))})", list(row.values()))
        return {"term_id": term_id, "alias": obs["surface_form"], "language": lang,
                "alias_type": alias_type, "jurisdiction": obs["jurisdiction"],
                "also_an_alias_of": others, "dry_run": dry_run}


def _decision_reference(ref: str) -> str:
    """A decision reference that resolves, or a Refusal naming the two accepted forms.

    Either a decision record under decisions/ that exists, or an owner ruling quoted
    exactly once in the ledger, written `references/project-standards.md :: "<quote>"`
    (the form dispose-adversarial-finding's OWNER-RULED disposition reads).
    """
    ref = (ref or "").strip()
    m = dbcore.LEDGER_REF_RE.match(ref)
    if m:
        dbcore.require_ledger_quote_once(m.group(1), "--decision-ref: the quote")
        return ref
    path = dbcore.resolve_under(dbcore.REPO_ROOT / "decisions", ref) if ref else None
    if path is not None and path.is_file():
        return ref
    raise Refusal(
        "--decision-ref must name the decision that reverses the declination: a decision "
        "record that exists under decisions/ (decisions/DR-....md), or an owner ruling as "
        "'references/project-standards.md :: \"<verbatim quote>\"', found once. Reversing "
        "a declination is a recorded decision (governance/decision-protocol.md), not an "
        f"edit. Got {ref!r}.")

    reader now exists: the cohort's vocabulary review (catalogue-plan-v2 section 3.4),
    which may find a declined term is a quantity after all. Retire in place (owner
    2026-09-16): revoked_at / revoked_by_session / revocation_reason are set (migration
    104) and every reader treats a revoked declination as absent -- add-parameter's
    declined-term refusal, research_batch_dod R16's 'disposed', the adversarial skill's
    declination query.

    (_decision_reference); a term with no declination; one already revoked.
    KNOWN LIMIT, stated: one declination row per term (the PRIMARY KEY), so a revoked
    declination cannot be followed by a second one; decline-parameter says so.

                  title_payload: str = None, session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Give a seeded ICF code the name CLAUDE.md section 6 requires it to be used with.

    GAP-ICF-TITLES is the subject: 43 of the 72 codes migration 081 seeded carry no title,
    because nothing in this repository states one and supplying it from memory is the act
    CLAUDE.md 5(c) forbids. This is the named path for closing that — retrieve the titles,
    persist the payload under `retrieval-log/`, and write them from the bytes.

    OVERWRITING A TITLE IS REFUSED. A title is a fact about an external classification, not
    a field to keep tidy; replacing one silently would erase whoever established it and the
    payload they established it from. A correction is a different act and owes its own
    reason.
    """
    icf_code = (icf_code or "").strip()
    title = (title or "").strip()
    if not title:
        raise Refusal("--title is required and may not be blank.")
    if not (title_source or title_payload):
        raise Refusal(
            "--title-source or --title-payload is required. A title with no source is a "
            "title from memory; the schema refuses the pair too.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        row = conn.execute(
            "SELECT icf_code, title, title_source FROM base_icf WHERE icf_code=?",
            [icf_code]).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise Refusal(
                f"{icf_code!r} is not in base_icf. Mint it first:\n"
                f"  db.py add-icf-code --icf-code {icf_code} --session ...")
        if row["title"]:
            raise Refusal(
                f"{icf_code} is already titled {row['title']!r} (source "
                f"{row['title_source']!r}). Overwriting would erase whoever established it "
                f"and the payload they established it from. A correction is a different "
                f"act and owes its own reason.")
        if title_payload:
            bodies = _payload_bodies(title_payload, "--title-payload",
                                     "a title is verified from BYTES or it records a "
                                     "document instead")
            if not any(title in b for b in bodies):
                raise Refusal(
                    f"--title {title!r} does not appear in {title_payload}. If the "
                    f"classification words it differently, use its wording.")
            title_source = f"payload:{title_payload}"
        conn.execute("UPDATE base_icf SET title=?, title_source=? WHERE icf_code=?",

-- 117_alias_observation_pointer.sql
-- SCHEMA migration -- a source-attested alias POINTS at the observation it came from.
--
-- Until now an alias's provenance was a substring of `notes` ("source-attested"), which
-- alias_provenance_audit read as text: any row whose free text contained the marker passed, and
-- the phrase, its quote and its source were copied into prose instead of reached by pointer
-- (CLAUDE.md rule 5; the plan scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/
-- base-population-plan.md, A3 and A17). The observation (observed_terms) already holds the phrase,
-- its language, locator and verbatim quote, and its ref_id reaches the source and so its
-- jurisdiction.
--
-- ONE NULLABLE COLUMN, ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN: NULL means "not attested by an observation"
-- (model-generated, curated, or recorded before the convention), which is what 2382 rows are.
-- `db.py add-alias` writes the pointer and may attach it to a row already held; the audit reads
-- the pointer. Nothing is backfilled: no existing row is attested by an observation.
-- Readers of term_aliases (re-derive with grep and sqlite_master): db.py, the audit above,
-- generate/search-query code that selects named columns. No view names the table.

input.body:
Tooling session plus governance records. **No research rows are written**: the only change to `data/guidebook.db` is schema migration 117 (`CLAUDE.md` rule 10: a schema-only bump is the ordinary shape of a tooling change).

## What this carries
- **Ledger** (`references/project-standards.md`): two dated entries recording the owner's 2026-11-06 statements. The 93 pre-reset item subjects are admitted as a basis under the existing "screen, then you approve" guard; the P1+P2+P3 language scope; every recommendation of the population plan's twelve owner decisions applied (E1, E3, E4 confirmed by name). One correction inside the first entry (no schema change is needed to admit the item catalogue, only a resolver).
- **Review and plan** (`scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/`): `base-review.md` and the Opus-written `base-population-plan.md`.
- **Tooling T1-T4** (`scripts/db.py`, migration 117):
  - T1: `items:<rowid>` catalogue entries for `mint-term-from-catalogue` (name must lie inside the item subject; no old item code reaches a live row) and a read-only `screen-item-catalogue`.
  - T2: `add-term` refuses a name that is not inside the observed phrase (OR-17; E1).
  - T3: `term_aliases.observation_id`; `add-alias` writes it, promotes an alias already held in place, refuses TRANSLATION; `alias_provenance_audit` classifies from the pointer, not the notes text.
  - T4: `set-icf-title --replace-reason` replaces a non-payload title with a payload-verified one, keeping the old one in notes; the payload check now anchors a title to its code.
  - `governance/schema-reference-exemptions.yaml`: the deliberate read of the archived `items` table.

## Checks
`scripts/preflight.sh`: PASS (56 green, 8 nothing-in-scope, 8 advisory failures). `test_scan_contract` fails G01 and G02, and fails them identically on untouched HEAD (verified in a worktree); the other advisory failures read nothing this diff touches (`validate_schema_cross_check` reports an archive-versus-code-leads mismatch for BS EN 81-70). New tests: AL06-AL09, T201-T202, T401-T404, M13-M15. `migrate_db.py --rebuild` reproduces schema 117 from scratch.

## Net-negative exception (`CLAUDE.md` section 8)
`git diff --shortstat origin/main -- scripts schemas .github skills ':!scripts/migrations'` → 3 files, +240/-28, of which about 70 lines are tests. It replaces no code. The additions are the refusals that make OR-17 and R11 enforceable and the writer the 2026-11-06 ruling requires. The plan's proposed deletions (the two alias-verification documents, hard-coded language lists in `skills/multilingual-research_SKILL.md`) touch doctrine or skills and are left for the owner to see first.

## Not in this PR
No term is minted, no parameter declined, no alias attested, no stakes written. The next PRs are research: the owner-approved screened table, the renames of terms that carry names no source used, the declinations of the axis and method terms, then open passes (plan sections C and D).

You are preparing the owner's APPROVAL PACK for the Accessible Built Environments Guidebook at /home/user/guidebook. You write one file; you write no database rows, you commit nothing, you push nothing, you do not run any db.py write verb or migration. Read-only Python only: sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro', uri=True) (no sqlite3 CLI exists). Start with `bash .claude/hooks/ensure-deps.sh`. CLAUDE.md governs everything; read it first (rules 0, 5, 7a, 8, 10; section 6 evidence model; section 7 traps).

## Context
The owner ruled on 2026-11-06 (last two entries of references/project-standards.md; read both in full): the 93 pre-reset item subjects, value-stripped and with old codes removed, are admitted as a BASIS for candidate parameter names under the guard "Screen, then you approve": every candidate is screened and listed in ONE table, and the owner approves that table in a dated ledger entry before any term is minted. The owner also applied the recommendations of scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/base-population-plan.md (read sections A, C.1, E and the rows on stakes and rooms in full; skim the rest). Tooling now exists (this branch): `python3 scripts/db.py screen-item-catalogue` prints, read-only, the 93 subjects with `items:<rowid>` pointers. It writes nothing; if a command you run would write, stop. The old item codes ([A-Z]-NN, e.g. a letter, hyphen, two digits) must NOT appear anywhere in your output file: the owner's ruling and the item-layer deletion (2026-09-01) forbid it; refer to items only as items:<rowid>. Item subjects are LEADS for quantities, never containers.

## Produce one file: /home/user/guidebook/scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/approval-pack.md
Four tables, each with a one-line key, a verdict-first sentence, and enough per-row warrant that the owner can approve or strike a row from a phone.

**Table 1 — the item subjects (93 rows, one per items:<rowid>).** Columns: entry_ref | stripped subject | kind (one of: quantity, element, intervention, method, setting, lens; a subject that names a thing to PROVIDE or a policy is an intervention) | prescription-bearing (yes/no; a condition clause or a whole prescription the value regex cannot see, e.g. 'at all', 'where', 'throughout', 'no X in Y') | held as (from the screen's held_as column) | recommendation | reason. Recommendation is exactly one of: MINT+PROMOTE (the subject itself names a measurable quantity that a code or study could assign a value to, it is not already held, and it is not prescription-bearing); MINT+DECLINE (an element or setting a term should record so the vocabulary is complete, but not a quantity: it is minted as a term then declined as a parameter with the stated reason); HOLD-LEAD (the subject implies a quantity but its words do not name it; record the implied quantity in the next column as prose, never as a name to mint, because minting it would coin a name: OR-17); REJECT (already held, prescription-bearing with no clean part, a method or lens, or not ours). HARD CONSTRAINT on every MINT row: the proposed canonical name must be a contiguous part of the stripped subject, character for character (case-insensitive), because `mint-term-from-catalogue` refuses anything else; show the proposed name in its own column and verify the containment by script, printing nothing that fails it. An element is never promoted to a parameter (OR-14). Do not mint 'items' that restate an already-held term under a new name: check each against terms and term_aliases in every language by exact and near match, and say which term answers it. Count how many rows fall in each recommendation using a script and print the command with the result (dated 2026-11-06).

**Table 2 — non-parameter terms (derive the set: every terms row that is not a base_parameters row and not an active parameter_declinations row).** For each: term_id | canonical_en | domain | kind | recommendation (DECLINE with reason, PROMOTE-CANDIDATE if it names a measurable quantity under determination, HOLD) | reason. The owner's E12 answer: the functional-axis terms and the method terms are declined as parameters, each with a reason, and kept as terms. Write each decline reason in one sentence from that term's own definition/scope_note in the DB (read them); do not invent definitions. Flag every term you judge a real quantity (for example one a code states a value for) as PROMOTE-CANDIDATE with a reason, so the owner can overrule a blanket decline; do not decline a term that is plainly a measurable design quantity. Look specifically at TERM-090 (level difference), TERM-092 (intermediate landing), TERM-093 (ramp usability), TERM-094 (accessibility audit), TERM-089 (already declined) and the hardware, acoustic, lighting, thermal and circulation terms.

**Table 3 — typical stakes (E9).** For each access_needs row with typical_stakes NULL (derive; expect 16): need_code | design_obligation (copy from the DB) | proposed stakes (one of the three values in access_stakes, read from the column's own CHECK) | warrant (one sentence quoting the design_obligation or the access_stakes definition it rests on) | confidence. These are the model's PROPOSALS, marked as such; the owner approves the table. A need that spans stakes gets the weakest-protection reading stated openly, not a hidden choice. Read the owner's rulings on stakes if any exist (git grep -n 'typical_stakes\|safety-critical' across references/ governance/ decisions/ with grep -r, since .ignore hides sessions/ from the Grep tool).

**Table 4 — renames (E2).** The terms whose canonical name is not inside the observed phrase they were minted from (derive with the NAMES-NEW join: term_adjudications → observed_terms → terms where instr(lower(surface_form), lower(canonical_en)) = 0). For each: term_id | current name | observed phrase and its language | proposed rename (the observed phrase, verbatim; if the observation is non-English the proposal is the phrase in its own language per owner E1) | what the verb needs (`rename-term`: read its code in scripts/db.py to say whether it can take the native phrase and what it does to the old name, and report honestly any gap you find) | flags. TERM-091 is parameter 12 and its rename needs the owner's quote on that parameter: mark it, do not propose around it.

## Rules
- Canadian English. Objective tone, verdict first, no flattery. Every count is the command that derives it plus its dated result; never a hand-typed standing figure (rule 7a).
- No invented names, translations, definitions, or citations. Where you illustrate in a language, mark [ILLUSTRATIVE, UNVERIFIED].
- Put the approving ledger wording the owner would paste at the end: a short block 'To approve: "approve table 1 rows N..., table 2 ..."' plus the instruction that approval is a dated entry in references/project-standards.md, after which the research session runs mint-term-from-catalogue per approved row, decline-parameter per declined term, set typical_stakes through a verb (check whether a verb exists: `grep -n typical_stakes scripts/db.py`; if none, say so as a GAP and propose nothing else), and rename-term per approved rename.
- Self-attack in five lines at the end: the likeliest ways this pack passes a bad row (a prescription the regex cannot see, an element minted as a parameter, a name that restates a held term in other words, a decline that hides a real quantity, a stakes warrant that overstates).
- Length tracks content; no recap. Tables use the Markdown pipe format.

Your reply to me: at most 12 lines: the verdict, the recommendation counts for Table 1 (from your script), anything that blocks approval or that the tooling cannot do, and the file path.

You are preparing the owner's APPROVAL PACK for the Accessible Built Environments Guidebook at /home/user/guidebook. You write one file; you write no database rows, you commit nothing, you push nothing, you do not run any db.py write verb or migration. Read-only Python only: sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro', uri=True) (no sqlite3 CLI exists). Start with `bash .claude/hooks/ensure-deps.sh`. CLAUDE.md governs everything; read it first (rules 0, 5, 7a, 8, 10; section 6 evidence model; section 7 traps).

## Context
The owner ruled on 2026-11-06 (last two entries of references/project-standards.md; read both in full): the 93 pre-reset item subjects, value-stripped and with old codes removed, are admitted as a BASIS for candidate parameter names under the guard "Screen, then you approve": every candidate is screened and listed in ONE table, and the owner approves that table in a dated ledger entry before any term is minted. The owner also applied the recommendations of scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/base-population-plan.md (read sections A, C.1, E and the rows on stakes and rooms in full; skim the rest). Tooling now exists (this branch): `python3 scripts/db.py screen-item-catalogue` prints, read-only, the 93 subjects with `items:<rowid>` pointers. It writes nothing; if a command you run would write, stop. The old item codes ([A-Z]-NN, e.g. a letter, hyphen, two digits) must NOT appear anywhere in your output file: the owner's ruling and the item-layer deletion (2026-09-01) forbid it; refer to items only as items:<rowid>. Item subjects are LEADS for quantities, never containers.

## Produce one file: /home/user/guidebook/scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/approval-pack.md
Four tables, each with a one-line key, a verdict-first sentence, and enough per-row warrant that the owner can approve or strike a row from a phone.

**Table 1 — the item subjects (93 rows, one per items:<rowid>).** Columns: entry_ref | stripped subject | kind (one of: quantity, element, intervention, method, setting, lens; a subject that names a thing to PROVIDE or a policy is an intervention) | prescription-bearing (yes/no; a condition clause or a whole prescription the value regex cannot see, e.g. 'at all', 'where', 'throughout', 'no X in Y') | held as (from the screen's held_as column) | recommendation | reason. Recommendation is exactly one of: MINT+PROMOTE (the subject itself names a measurable quantity that a code or study could assign a value to, it is not already held, and it is not prescription-bearing); MINT+DECLINE (an element or setting a term should record so the vocabulary is complete, but not a quantity: it is minted as a term then declined as a parameter with the stated reason); HOLD-LEAD (the subject implies a quantity but its words do not name it; record the implied quantity in the next column as prose, never as a name to mint, because minting it would coin a name: OR-17); REJECT (already held, prescription-bearing with no clean part, a method or lens, or not ours). HARD CONSTRAINT on every MINT row: the proposed canonical name must be a contiguous part of the stripped subject, character for character (case-insensitive), because `mint-term-from-catalogue` refuses anything else; show the proposed name in its own column and verify the containment by script, printing nothing that fails it. An element is never promoted to a parameter (OR-14). Do not mint 'items' that restate an already-held term under a new name: check each against terms and term_aliases in every language by exact and near match, and say which term answers it. Count how many rows fall in each recommendation using a script and print the command with the result (dated 2026-11-06).

**Table 2 — non-parameter terms (derive the set: every terms row that is not a base_parameters row and not an active parameter_declinations row).** For each: term_id | canonical_en | domain | kind | recommendation (DECLINE with reason, PROMOTE-CANDIDATE if it names a measurable quantity under determination, HOLD) | reason. The owner's E12 answer: the functional-axis terms and the method terms are declined as parameters, each with a reason, and kept as terms. Write each decline reason in one sentence from that term's own definition/scope_note in the DB (read them); do not invent definitions. Flag every term you judge a real quantity (for example one a code states a value for) as PROMOTE-CANDIDATE with a reason, so the owner can overrule a blanket decline; do not decline a term that is plainly a measurable design quantity. Look specifically at TERM-090 (level difference), TERM-092 (intermediate landing), TERM-093 (ramp usability), TERM-094 (accessibility audit), TERM-089 (already declined) and the hardware, acoustic, lighting, thermal and circulation terms.

**Table 3 — typical stakes (E9).** For each access_needs row with typical_stakes NULL (derive; expect 16): need_code | design_obligation (copy from the DB) | proposed stakes (one of the three values in access_stakes, read from the column's own CHECK) | warrant (one sentence quoting the design_obligation or the access_stakes definition it rests on) | confidence. These are the model's PROPOSALS, marked as such; the owner approves the table. A need that spans stakes gets the weakest-protection reading stated openly, not a hidden choice. Read the owner's rulings on stakes if any exist (git grep -n 'typical_stakes\|safety-critical' across references/ governance/ decisions/ with grep -r, since .ignore hides sessions/ from the Grep tool).

**Table 4 — renames (E2).** The terms whose canonical name is not inside the observed phrase they were minted from (derive with the NAMES-NEW join: term_adjudications → observed_terms → terms where instr(lower(surface_form), lower(canonical_en)) = 0). For each: term_id | current name | observed phrase and its language | proposed rename (the observed phrase, verbatim; if the observation is non-English the proposal is the phrase in its own language per owner E1) | what the verb needs (`rename-term`: read its code in scripts/db.py to say whether it can take the native phrase and what it does to the old name, and report honestly any gap you find) | flags. TERM-091 is parameter 12 and its rename needs the owner's quote on that parameter: mark it, do not propose around it.

## Rules
- Canadian English. Objective tone, verdict first, no flattery. Every count is the command that derives it plus its dated result; never a hand-typed standing figure (rule 7a).
- No invented names, translations, definitions, or citations. Where you illustrate in a language, mark [ILLUSTRATIVE, UNVERIFIED].
- Put the approving ledger wording the owner would paste at the end: a short block 'To approve: "approve table 1 rows N..., table 2 ..."' plus the instruction that approval is a dated entry in references/project-standards.md, after which the research session runs mint-term-from-catalogue per approved row, decline-parameter per declined term, set typical_stakes through a verb (check whether a verb exists: `grep -n typical_stakes scripts/db.py`; if none, say so as a GAP and propose nothing else), and rename-term per approved rename.
- Self-attack in five lines at the end: the likeliest ways this pack passes a bad row (a prescription the regex cannot see, an element minted as a parameter, a name that restates a held term in other words, a decline that hides a real quantity, a stakes warrant that overstates).
- Length tracks content; no recap. Tables use the Markdown pipe format.

Your reply to me: at most 12 lines: the verdict, the recommendation counts for Table 1 (from your script), anything that blocks approval or that the tooling cannot do, and the file path.

- **Ledger:** your answers are recorded in `references/project-standards.md`, with "e1 e3 e4; Appy yes" quoted as the confirmation of those three. I read "Appy" as "Apply", and wrote that reading into the entry. The entry treats the rest of your blanket "apply all recommendations" as choosing the plan's recommended option on E2 and E5–E12. It also states that the blanket reading does not approve the item table, the stakes table or the renames themselves.
- **Tooling in PR #213:**
  - **Item subjects:** they can be minted from by row number (`items:<rowid>`), and the name must lie inside the subject. A read-only `screen-item-catalogue` lists them with no old codes.
  - **Names:** `add-term` now refuses a name that isn't inside the phrase the source used.
  - **Aliases:** migration 117 adds an alias-to-observation pointer. `add-alias` attaches it, promoting a held alias in place and refusing TRANSLATION. `alias_provenance_audit` now classifies from the pointer, not from the notes text.
  - **ICF titles:** `set-icf-title --replace-reason` replaces a non-WHO title with one checked against the payload and next to its code. The old title is kept in notes.
- **Checks:** `scripts/preflight.sh` passes. A scratch rebuild reproduces schema 117. I added 13 tests and they pass.
- **Failures in `test_scan_contract`:** G01 and G02 fail, and they fail the same way on untouched HEAD. The other advisory failures read nothing I changed.
- **Net-negative:** the scripts diff is +240/−28 lines, about 70 of them tests. It replaces no code, and the PR description names that exception. I did not touch the plan's proposed deletions (the two alias-verification documents and the hard-coded language lists in the multilingual-research skill), because they are doctrine and skill text you should see first.
- **Open as of now:** the Opus agent is writing `scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/approval-pack.md` with four tables: the 93 item subjects, a decline-or-promote call for each non-parameter term, the stakes proposals for the 16 needs, and the renames. I'll report when it lands.

After you approve the tables in a dated ledger entry, the next steps are research changes: the mints, declinations, renames and stakes. Those go in separate PRs, and the PR with the tooling needs to merge first (rule 10). I won't merge anything.

                            observation, adjudicated to THIS term, whose surface form
                            contains the new name (the 2026-09-09 rule, kept by the owner
                            on 2026-10-09: names come from observed phrases);
      --ruling-quote "..."  or from the owner's own words, quoted verbatim and found
                            exactly once in references/project-standards.md, containing

The approval pack is written and pushed to PR #213. It proposes rows only. Nothing is minted, declined, renamed or written until you approve it in a dated ledger entry.

The pack is `scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/approval-pack.md`. I read it in full. Its counts come from its own grep command, and a script confirmed that every proposed name sits inside its item subject.

- **Item subjects (93):**
  - **Mint and promote:** 2 (`flicker` and `slip resistance`).
  - **Mint then decline as non-quantities:** 12 (elements and settings such as acoustic door, landmark and platform lift).
  - **Hold as a lead:** 30. The implied quantity is described in prose, not minted, so no name is coined (OR-17).
  - **Reject:** 49. Most were already held as terms.
- **The other 83 terms:** 78 decline with a reason, 3 flagged as real quantities you may want promoted (TERM-049 acoustic absorption, TERM-050 speech intelligibility, TERM-090 level difference), and 2 hold.
- **Stakes for the 16 needs:** 14 exclusion, 1 safety-critical (A-STABLE), 1 friction. Four rows take the weaker-protection reading over a harm their own wording touches (A-NOSIGHT, A-NOSOUND, A-EFFORT, A-SIZE); look at those first.
- **Renames:** TERM-090 to `niveauverschillen`, TERM-092 to `tussenbordes`, and TERM-093 to `usability`, the last with a warning that the bare word is wider than its definition. TERM-091 (parameter 12) is held for your quote and not proposed.

The pack ends with a paste-ready approval sentence, from which you can strike any row. Approval is a dated entry in `references/project-standards.md` whose heading occurs once. The mints need that heading as their `--approval-ref`.

The pack's builder found three tooling defects; two are fixed:
1. **Screen:** `screen-item-catalogue` failed on the canonical database. That was my bug (`connect(True)` is dry-run, not read-only). It is fixed, and an unclosed bracket in one item subject is now stripped.
2. **Rename:** `rename-term` refused any non-English observation, which contradicted your E1 answer. It now accepts one, with test N10b.
3. **Stakes (open, not built):** no verb writes `typical_stakes`, so approving the stakes table changes nothing yet. I did not add one, because nothing reads the field today (rule 8). Say so if you want it built anyway.

`scripts/preflight.sh` still passes. The two `test_scan_contract` failures (G01 and G02) are the same ones that fail on untouched HEAD.

Each mint needs a definition (`--definition`), and the catalogue supplies none, so that text would be model prose. I'd show it to you before any mint.

Rule 10 means PR #213 (tooling) has to merge before the research PRs that write rows. I will not merge it.
