## Owner rulings 2026-11-06 — minimise code; no net-negative requirement

Given in this session (https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iMkXnQsEwzR9oaTqn1), in three messages after the gap register for the two pipeline batches was filed and handed to an analyst, and recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Each is quoted verbatim, including its lower case:

- (question) "net negative rule? that is supposed to be reserved for minimizing code infrastructure?"
- "we want to MINIMIZE code wherever possible. we don't require a net negative because the extreme of that means we end up with no code"
- "we want the bare essentials in the most code efficient manner possible so that we are agile and lean"

**What this does.** The readings are the assistant's and are marked; the owner's words above are the ruling.

1. **The standing constraint is minimal code, not a shrinking total.** The 2026-10-12 direction (as little code as possible) stands and is sharpened to the bare essentials written as efficiently as possible. The net-negative requirement that operationalised it (a PR touching `scripts/`, `schemas/`, `.github/` or `skills/` may not raise their line total without naming the exception) is not required. [ASSUMPTION: the net-negative bullet is read as a rule about code infrastructure only, as the owner's question puts it, so it never applied to research rows, owner decisions, doctrine or prose.]
2. **What stays.** The tests of `CLAUDE.md` section 8 that need no count: before adding a check, script or table, state what wrong thing reaches the guidebook without it; nothing is added without naming what reads it. [ASSUMPTION: "wherever possible" is a standing preference weighed case by case, not a gate, so a defect that reaches the guidebook is still fixed with the smallest code that closes it.]
3. **Supersession.** The net-negative bullet of `CLAUDE.md` section 8 is rewritten in place, as that file's own rule directs (fix the sentence, put the account in the commit message). No `SUPERSEDES` pair is written for it: the audit anchors on a target quote that must still occur once, and the sentence it would quote no longer exists. The simplification plan's W3 (`workplan/2026-10-12-simplification-workplan.md`) and the "net-negative" item of the standing constraints and W1-W10 list in `workplan/2026-10-23-pipeline-resolution-workplan.md` restate the old bullet; they are plans, left as written, and this ruling governs where they differ.

**What is unblocked, and what still waits.** Nothing waits on the owner. The Opus resolution analysis of GAP-074 to GAP-096 was told of the ruling and is to classify each tooling recommendation as close-as-accepted, rule or prose, reuse, delete or new code.

CONDITION: any session writing or reviewing a PR that touches `scripts/`, `schemas/`, `.github/` or `skills/`, or asked whether a change must reduce the line total.
ACTION: (1) Do not require or claim a net-negative total. Name what the added code reads and what wrong thing reaches the guidebook without it, and name any code it replaces or makes deletable. (2) Try, in order: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect. (3) Treat every [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/research/retrieval_log.py — persist what was actually retrieved.

WHY
---
On 2026-08-19 the first research batch after the restart wrote FABRICATED author
lists onto all five of its admissions, and stamped them
`verification_status='VERIFIED'`, `verified_by_tool='crossref'`,
`verification_method='tool'`, `metadata_quality='COMPLETE'`.

The retrieval had genuinely happened — the reference counts stored alongside match
Crossref exactly, and those numbers exist nowhere but that payload. The author
array was in the same JSON object and was overwritten from memory.

Nothing could detect it, for one structural reason:

    verification_method='tool' was a SELF-ASSERTION WITH NO ARTEFACT BEHIND IT.

No gate could tell an executed retrieval from a claimed one, because the evidence
of the retrieval was never kept. Finding it took an adversarial pass and five
agents. With the payload on disk it is a one-line diff.

Owner ruling, 2026-08-19: "the repository has more than enough room to store
scratchpad logs if they're ever needed. it is very unlikely we will ever have to
look through them unless we are auditing for fidelity."

That is exactly the value profile of this log — near-zero read frequency, and
irreplaceable in the one case that matters.

USE
---
    from retrieval_log import fetch
    payload = fetch("https://api.crossref.org/works/10.xxxx/yyy", session=S,
                    purpose="crossref metadata for REF-00965")

`fetch` returns the parsed JSON *and* writes the raw bytes under
`retrieval-log/<session>/`, with a manifest line recording url, sha256, byte
count, HTTP status, and the UTC timestamp. Writes happen BEFORE the caller sees
the data, so a caller cannot log a different payload than the one it acted on.
`fetch` returns None -- but STILL writes the artefact and manifest line -- for a
non-2xx status as well as for a transport failure or an unparseable body: a 404
or a publisher interstitial is retrieved evidence of a failed retrieval, not
absence of evidence, and CLAUDE.md 5(c) is the reason that distinction is kept
rather than dropped along with the rest of the failure.

    python3 scripts/research/retrieval_log.py --verify-authors --session <id>

verifies stored authors against the LOGGED payload — offline, no network, and
authoritative as-of-retrieval rather than as-of-audit. That distinction matters:
re-fetching at audit time cannot detect a record that was correct when written and
has since been corrected upstream, nor can it run when the API is unreachable.
"""

import codecs
import hashlib
import html
import json
import os

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/research/retrieval_log.py — persist what was actually retrieved.

WHY
---
On 2026-08-19 the first research batch after the restart wrote FABRICATED author
lists onto all five of its admissions, and stamped them
`verification_status='VERIFIED'`, `verified_by_tool='crossref'`,
`verification_method='tool'`, `metadata_quality='COMPLETE'`.

The retrieval had genuinely happened — the reference counts stored alongside match
Crossref exactly, and those numbers exist nowhere but that payload. The author
array was in the same JSON object and was overwritten from memory.

Nothing could detect it, for one structural reason:

    verification_method='tool' was a SELF-ASSERTION WITH NO ARTEFACT BEHIND IT.

No gate could tell an executed retrieval from a claimed one, because the evidence
of the retrieval was never kept. Finding it took an adversarial pass and five
agents. With the payload on disk it is a one-line diff.

Owner ruling, 2026-08-19: "the repository has more than enough room to store
scratchpad logs if they're ever needed. it is very unlikely we will ever have to
look through them unless we are auditing for fidelity."

That is exactly the value profile of this log — near-zero read frequency, and
irreplaceable in the one case that matters.

USE
---
    from retrieval_log import fetch
    payload = fetch("https://api.crossref.org/works/10.xxxx/yyy", session=S,
                    purpose="crossref metadata for REF-00965")

`fetch` returns the parsed JSON *and* writes the raw bytes under
`retrieval-log/<session>/`, with a manifest line recording url, sha256, byte
count, HTTP status, and the UTC timestamp. Writes happen BEFORE the caller sees
the data, so a caller cannot log a different payload than the one it acted on.
`fetch` returns None -- but STILL writes the artefact and manifest line -- for a
non-2xx status as well as for a transport failure or an unparseable body: a 404
or a publisher interstitial is retrieved evidence of a failed retrieval, not
absence of evidence, and CLAUDE.md 5(c) is the reason that distinction is kept
rather than dropped along with the rest of the failure.

    python3 scripts/research/retrieval_log.py --verify-authors --session <id>

verifies stored authors against the LOGGED payload — offline, no network, and
authoritative as-of-retrieval rather than as-of-audit. That distinction matters:
re-fetching at audit time cannot detect a record that was correct when written and
has since been corrected upstream, nor can it run when the API is unreachable.
"""

CSA/ASC B651 Accessible Design for the Built Environment - Accessibility Standards Canada
This standard contains requirements for making buildings and other facilities accessible to individuals with a range of physical, sensory, and cognitive disabilities. It is a new edition of a previous standard. It addresses the design aspects of physical spaces and the elements within them to remove barriers to access, including:
updated dimensions for platforms, tactile direction indicator positioning, and more, based on current data from anthropometric research;
a detailed explanation of luminance (colour) contrast and its application;
updated guidance on addressing functional and cognitive barriers;
revised guidance for the controls and sizes of power-assisted doors; and,
updated recommendations for water bottle filling stations and controls.
This standard is referenced in the National Building Code and other legislation across Canada.

Overview
Overview
Considering accessibility in the design of products, systems, environments, and facilities is key to ensuring equity for all Canadians. Removing barriers to accessibility makes products easier to use for people with disabilities. Plus, many accessibility features benefit those who do not have a disability by creating more usable and customizable design. More than one in five (22%) Canadians aged 15 and over, an estimated 6.2 million people, have one or more disabilities1. With this in mind, removing accessibility barriers is not only beneficial, but it makes good business sense to increase access for all customers, including those with disabilities.
The CSA/ASC B651, Accessible design for the built environment standard, is a revision of a previously existing standard. It contains requirements for making buildings and other facilities accessible to individuals with physical, sensory, and/or cognitive disabilities.
CSA/ASC B651 addresses the design aspects of physical spaces and the elements within them to remove barriers to access. The new edition of the standard was developed by the CSA Accessibility for the Built Environment Technical Subcommittee, under the jurisdiction of the Technical Committee on Accessibility, and funded by Accessibility Standards Canada.
The updates to CSA/ASC B651 include the following major changes:
•	updated dimensions based on current data from anthropometric research;
•	notes to assist in the interpretation of the standard’s requirements;
•	a detailed explanation of luminance (colour) contrast;
•	revised accessibility guidance for the application of luminance (colour) contrast;
•	revised guidance for tactile direction indicator positioning;
•	updated guidance on addressing functional and cognitive barriers;
•	revised guidance for controls for power-assisted doors;
•	additional guidance for the minimum platform size of platform lifts that form part of an accessible path of travel;
•	updated recommendations for water bottle filling stations; and
•	revised guidance for water fountain controls
Footnote
S. Morris, G. Fawcett, L. Brisebois and J. Hughes. November 2018.
“A demographic, employment and income profile of Canadians with disabilities aged 15 years and over, 2017”.

Les résultats confirment que la version 4.0 du RHFAC est en français, avec deux documents clés.

- **Guide en français (v 4.0, janvier 2024)** : le guide officiel de la FRH en français existe, avec une annexe consacrée au sondage d'évaluation et une section sur le programme version 4.0 (Guide pour la certification en matière d'accessibilité de la FRH, v 4.0 (janvier 2024)).
- **Sondage d'évaluation en français (v 4.0, septembre 2024)** : une version française du sondage est publiée sous le titre « Sondage d'évaluation | v 4.0 (septembre 2024) ». Elle présente les niveaux de certification et les exigences, ainsi que les catégories d'évaluation (par exemple l'accessibilité des véhicules). Le programme propose deux niveaux : la certification standard et la certification Or (Le Programme RHFAC propose deux niveaux de certification : la certification en matière d'accessibilité de la FRH et la certification OR en matière d'accessibilité de la FRH.). Une variante pré-construction existe aussi.
- **Date d'entrée en vigueur** : selon le site anglophone de la FRH, the new RHFAC Rating Survey v4.0 was made available effective January 15, 2024.

Seuils de certification : la page française de la FRH indique qu'une note de 60 % à 79 % correspond à la certification standard, et qu'une note de plus de 79 % correspond à la certification Or (Avez-vous obtenu une note entre 60 % et 79 % au sondage d'évaluation du Programme RHFAC? ... Avez-vous obtenu une note de plus de 79 % au sondage d'évaluation du Programme RHFAC?). Le sondage français indique le seuil de 80 % et plus pour la certification standard, ce qui diffère légèrement de la page de la FRH. Il faudrait vérifier la version officielle avant de citer un seuil précis.

Autres points : le guide de désignation des professionnels RHFAC est en version 1.5 (septembre 2024) et précise que the electronic version will prevail en cas d'écart avec la version imprimée. Une formation de base en français a été lancée au cours de l'exercice 2023-2024 (rapport annuel de la FRH).

Non trouvé : je n'ai pas trouvé de document de référence précisant les différences entre la v4.0 et la v3.0 dans les résultats. Le PDF officiel du guide français et le sondage français sont les meilleures sources à consulter directement.

## Owner statements 2026-11-06 (third) — the register is written in English first, then translated to search each language; it must not be English-biased

Given in session https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iPbFEPovMCoes1oKx9 while the RHFAC Rating Survey v4.0 and the CSA/ASC B651 listing were being catalogued, and recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim; times in session order.

> "we have categories according to the kind of technique (acoustic, circulation, etc) as well as categories according to building typology and room"

> "and these cross-pollinate each other"

> "what appears in a category specification for type (eg circulation, acoustics) will appear in building typologies and rooms and vice versa"

> "you don't need French edition here"

> "what I mean is that you will build out a comprehensive register of concepts/items/terms/techniques but you have to ensure that you research them across all of our chosen jurisdictions and languages without an English bias"

> "so we are doing prep work to get this all written out in English and then we have to translate it all properly into other languages to search them too"

**What this establishes**

1. **Two category axes that derive from one set of rows.** A technique category (acoustic, circulation …) and a building typology or room are two views of the same criteria. Whatever sits in a technique category appears under the typologies and rooms that use it, and the reverse. Neither view is maintained beside the other (`CLAUDE.md` rules 5 and 8): both are generated from one table of tagged criteria.
2. **English first, as preparation.** The English register is the search plan, not the vocabulary. It is not definitive: the RHFAC survey is a Canadian rating instrument that scores criteria by points and states no values, and the B651 text was not obtained.
3. **Translation is for searching.** A translation of the English register is a search seed, produced to be in use in the jurisdiction and not word for word ("properly"), and recorded as model-generated and flagged, which is what OR-12b permits. It is not a term, not an alias and not evidence. It becomes vocabulary only when an instrument of that language is read and the phrase is found there (E4; OR-17; R11).
4. **The register must not end where English ends.** A concept English does not carve out cannot be reached by translating English. The register therefore also takes concepts from native-language open passes over each P1+P2+P3 instrument (OR-13; plan C.3), named by the instrument's own phrase (E1), and records, per concept and per language-and-jurisdiction pair, whether it was searched and what was found, including absence.
5. **The French RHFAC edition is not used here.** It was retrieved before this statement and is persisted in the retrieval log; nothing is drawn from it.

[ASSUMPTION: "translate it all properly" is read as OR-12b's generation of in-use, jurisdiction-specific terms for flagged searches, and not as licence to store translations as vocabulary; the owner's earlier OR-17 ("It is not acceptable for the model to generate its own phrases/names/aliases") and E4 are not read as withdrawn.]

CONDITION: any session asking whether the English register may be translated into other languages, what a translation of it is, whether it may be stored as aliases, how a concept English does not name enters the register, or how technique categories relate to building typologies and rooms.
ACTION: (1) Generate both category views from one tagged table. (2) Treat every translated term as a flagged model-generated search seed, never as vocabulary. (3) Promote a seed only by reading an instrument in its language and finding the phrase there. (4) Feed concepts found in native-language readings back into the register by the instrument's own phrase. (5) Treat every [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.
DATE: 2026-11-06 — owner statements, quoted above.

The RHFAC survey and the B651 listing are catalogued, and three pilot terminology passes (Japanese/JP, German/DE, French/FR) are running in the background. I'll report when they finish. Nothing has been written to the database. The catalogue is in `scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/rhfac-b651-catalogue.md`.

**What was and wasn't read**
- **RHFAC Rating Survey v4.0:** read in full. It has 640 criteria across 70 sections in 12 chapters, and each criterion carries technique tags and a place (room, element or typology). Two of the survey's own section totals disagree with its criteria: 8.12 states 19 against 17 summed, and 8.13 states 24 against 22. I kept them as printed.
- **CSA/ASC B651:** I did not read the standard itself. It is a paid, copy-protected PDF of 283 pages in English and 307 in French. I read the ASC listing page and the CSA store page, which give the scope and the 2023 changes.
- **The survey states no dimensions, forces, slopes or times.** Those sit in the codes it rates against. The catalogue is a source of concepts and techniques to search for, not values.

**Your two category axes.** Both are generated from one tagged table, `rhfac-criteria.tsv`, so neither is kept by hand and what sits in a technique category appears under the rooms and typologies that use it. The catalogue shows both directions (technique × kind of place, and place → techniques). The technique tags come from keyword rules on the criterion's own words, so treat them as leads.

**What the register shows**
- **Shared concepts:** 32 concepts recur in three or more sections, led by "well-illuminated" in 37 sections. Slip resistance, drainage, nosing, riser and tread, and edge protection have no term in the base.
- **Typologies and rooms:** the survey frames many typologies and rooms the base's 17 rooms don't cover (pool, library, lodging, retail, playground, trail and others).
- **Coverage:** coverage of this register is 0 today. No concept has a research cell, and the language half of a source can't be derived because `evidence_sources.language` is NULL on every row.

**Your direction on method.** I recorded it as a third dated ledger entry. English is the search plan. Translations are flagged model-generated search seeds (OR-12b) and never vocabulary. A seed becomes an attested alias only when an instrument in that language is read and the phrase is found in it. Each pass also reads the instrument in full for concepts the English register lacks, named by the instrument's own phrase. Without that step, translating English would miss any concept English doesn't name.

**Pilot passes.** Each pass retrieves and persists its national instruments, reads them in the original language, and logs queries with prior expectations. Each writes observations, coverage, concepts the English register lacks, flagged seeds, and the defects it finds in the method. They write only under `scratchpad/…/terminology-pass/<pair>/` and the retrieval log. DIN 18040 and paywalled JIS or AFNOR standards will be logged as not obtainable and not reconstructed from memory. I chose three structurally different languages so method defects show up before all 14 run. The rows can only ship after PR #213 merges (rule 10).

- **Branch:** I'll commit the passes' outputs to the same branch. Once PR #213 merges, the research rows need a branch restarted from `main`.
- **French RHFAC:** I retrieved the French RHFAC survey and guide before you said they weren't needed. They are in the retrieval log, and nothing is drawn from them.
- **Terms-held column:** the catalogue's "held in the base today" column is a crude English substring match. Many entries read "not checked", so don't read it as a gap analysis.

content.text:
I digested B651:23 by headers only and added it to the catalogue as section 2.4. The retry after your sharing change returned the PDF itself: CSA/ASC B651:23, revised June 2025, 283 pages. I read the table of contents, 58 defined-term names, clause 1.6, the opening of 4.7, and the headings of Annexes A to F. I did not read the body clauses, so no dimension, force, slope or time is recorded. The digest is in `rhfac-b651-catalogue.md`, with the full heading list and pages in `scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/b651-headings.tsv` (232 headings).

**Decision for you:** the PDF's legal notice allows loading it for review, search, browse and print. It says users may not "make an electronic copy". The project's rule that every source be persisted conflicts with that. I kept the PDF out of git (excluded locally), and only its retrieval line, hash and the heading-level digest are in the repository. Whether the project may hold the PDF is a licensing question for you.

**What the headers show**
- **Exterior and public realm:** B651 covers this far more fully than RHFAC. It has clauses on pedestrian crossings, intersections, transit stops, urban furniture, landscaping, temporary works, and trails and beach access in Annex D.
- **Technique topics:** it gives several their own clauses where RHFAC scores one criterion. These include luminance contrast, tactile walking surface indicators, headroom and protruding objects, door-opening force, power-assisted doors, handrail grip, and slip potential in Annex B.
- **Annex A:** it puts the human body into the standard through reach ranges, long white cane detection space, service dog space, wheeled device dimensions and turning areas.
- **Clause 4.7:** it names functional and cognitive barriers, environmental intolerances and acoustics as recommendations, not requirements. The question for the native-language readings is whether other jurisdictions treat these as clauses, recommendations or not at all.

**Caveats**
- The test for B651 headings RHFAC doesn't name is a crude word-stem match and over-reports gaps. It flags "Headroom" although RHFAC's "Height clearance" is the same concept in other words.
- I had typed a made-up hash prefix for the PDF into the catalogue and replaced it with the real one before committing. The earlier catalogue commits never contained it.

The Japanese, German and French passes are still running. Everything is pushed to PR #213.

# Terminology research pass: shared brief

You run ONE terminology pass for the Accessible Built Environments Guidebook (`/home/user/guidebook`) for the language-and-jurisdiction pair your instruction names. It is part of a wave over the P1+P2+P3 languages. Pilot passes already exist (`terminology-pass/FR-FR/`, and DE-DE and JA-JP if finished); read `FR-FR/pass-record.md` and look at its `build.py`, which you may copy and adapt as your verifier.

Read `CLAUDE.md` first (rules 0, 5, 7a, 8, 10; section 5 failure modes; section 7 traps incl. the Wayback route), and the three entries headed "Owner statements 2026-11-06" and the fourth in `references/project-standards.md`.

## What this is and is not
- The English register is the SEARCH PLAN, not the vocabulary, and it is Canadian English from one rating instrument (RHFAC), digested in `rhfac-b651-catalogue.md` (sections 2 to 6), `rhfac-criteria.tsv` (640 criteria) and `b651-headings.tsv` (the CSA/ASC B651:23 clause structure). It is a guideline, not definitive.
- Rendering the register into your language produces FLAGGED, MODEL-GENERATED SEARCH SEEDS (owner OR-12b: terms you believe are IN USE in that jurisdiction, never word for word). Seeds point the reading and are never findings, never aliases, never vocabulary.
- A FINDING is a phrase VERBATIM in a retrieved text of that jurisdiction in its own language, with locator and a quote that verifies in the saved bytes.
- The register must not end where English ends: read the instrument IN FULL in its own language and record every design quantity, element, technique and defined category it treats, including ones the register lacks (reverse harvest; owner E1: a concept first met outside English is named by the instrument's own phrase, never an English gloss).
- Terminology only: do not extract values as findings.

## Concept list
Use the 32 concepts recurring in three or more sections (catalogue 2.1), the quantity-bearing words (2.2), the base's active parameters (`select p.parameter_id, t.canonical_en from base_parameters p join terms t using(term_id)`), and the B651 clause headings that RHFAC does not name (`b651-headings.tsv`, last column). Existing aliases in your language (`select alias, alias_type, jurisdiction, notes from term_aliases where lower(language)='<code>'`) are MODEL-GENERATED SEEDS, never findings.

## Lessons from the French pilot (apply them)
1. A text match is not a sense match. Record FOUND only where the instrument uses the phrase in the register concept's sense; say so in the note. "inclinaison" appearing in an unrelated sense is not a finding.
2. The register is criterion-shaped: near-duplicate rows share observations. Count distinct phrases as well as observations, and do not let near-duplicates inflate FOUND.
3. The instrument may split or merge concepts differently (the French fixed ramp is a different word from "rampe"; its corridor is not "couloir"). Record the carve difference; do not force a one-to-one map.
4. The drafting structure itself may differ (aim then prescription, defined categories, equivalent-effect routes). Note it in the pass record.
5. Held aliases that are word-for-word translations and occur in no instrument should be reported as such.
6. Instrument lists cannot be derived from the base for most pairs. Say how you built yours and what you could not derive.

## Procedure
1. **Instruments.** Primary accessibility instruments for buildings in force, current editions only, free official texts first (the national law and regulation portal, the building authority's published code). Derive candidates from `research_code_leads`, `references/standards-registry.md` and `select ref_id, pub_title, standard_number from evidence_sources where jurisdiction='<J>'`, then search. A paywalled standard you cannot retrieve is NOT-OBTAINABLE: log the attempt; do not substitute memory of its content.
2. **Retrieve and persist** from the repository ROOT (retrieval_log writes relative to cwd; running it elsewhere misplaces artefacts):
   `cd /home/user/guidebook && python3 - <<'PY'` / `import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts/research'); import retrieval_log as r; r.fetch(URL, session='session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review', purpose='terminology pass <PAIR>: <what>')` / `PY`.
   fetch() returns None for non-JSON but persists the bytes and a manifest line under `retrieval-log/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/`. A publisher block or a JavaScript shell: use the Wayback `if_` route (CLAUDE.md section 7), as the French pass did for Légifrance. Extract text with `pdftotext -layout` or by stripping tags; save the text to `terminology-pass/<PAIR>/text/<artefact-sha-prefix>.txt` and record its sha256. Never disable TLS verification or unset the proxy. The owner has ruled that retrieved standards may be held in the repository.
3. **Read each retrieved instrument in full**, in its own language. Locate with scripts, read the located passages yourself, and record honestly what you read and what you did not [SKIPPED: part, why]. Image-only diagrams are unread.
4. **Record** under `scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/terminology-pass/<PAIR>/` (PAIR like `DA-DK`):
   - `search-log.md`: every query verbatim, a prior expectation written BEFORE the result, the result, and a note on query shape (R14). Keep empties.
   - `instruments.tsv`: title as written, issuing body, edition in force, URL, sha256 of retrieved bytes, retrieval status, read in full yes/no/partly with what was skipped.
   - `observations.tsv`: concept (register label or REVERSE-HARVEST), phrase VERBATIM, language, instrument, locator, context quote verbatim, text file, quote_verified_in_text, note (ours).
   - `coverage.tsv`: one row per register concept: FOUND / FOUND-PARTIAL / SEARCHED-ABSENT (instrument read in full, concept not treated) / NOT-OBTAINABLE / NOT-READ, with a note.
   - `reverse-harvest.tsv`: what the instrument treats that no register row names, in its own phrase; any gloss clearly marked as ours.
   - `seeds.tsv`: model-generated seeds for register concepts NOT found, flagged MODEL-GENERATED, with the jurisdiction they are meant to be in use in. Short.
   - `build.py` (adapted from the French pass) that regenerates the TSVs and exits 1 on any quote not found verbatim in the saved text.
   - `pass-record.md` (verdict first, at most 80 lines): retrieved and read, not read and why, counts by script (command beside each), where this language's instrument carves the field differently from English, method defects, and a self-attack of the five likeliest ways the record is wrong.
5. **Hard prohibitions.** Do not write `data/guidebook.db` or run any `db.py` write verb or migration. Do not commit or push. Do not edit `CLAUDE.md` or any file outside your `terminology-pass/<PAIR>/` folder and `retrieval-log/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/`. Invent no citation, article number, URL or quotation; every locator and quote must come from bytes you retrieved. Use no pre-reset item codes (a letter, a hyphen, two digits). Do not use the French RHFAC edition. Canadian English in your own prose; objective tone, no flattery.

Budget: depth on the one or two principal instruments over breadth. Stop when they are read in full and recorded, or when an unavoidable block is logged. Reply in at most 12 lines: verdict, instruments read in full vs not, counts (FOUND / FOUND-PARTIAL / ABSENT / REVERSE-HARVEST), the two most surprising carve differences with English, method defects, and the folder path.

Eleven passes are running in the background, one for each remaining language. They are Danish, Spanish, Finnish, Italian, Korean, Dutch, Norwegian, Portuguese, Swedish, Chinese, and an English-variants pass. Japanese and German, from the first pilot wave, are still running. Together that covers the 14 languages.

- **Shared brief:** every pass follows `scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/terminology-pass/BRIEF.md`. It carries the French pilot's lessons:
  - A phrase counts as found only where the instrument uses it in the register concept's sense.
  - Distinct phrases are counted separately from observations, because near-duplicate criteria inflate the observation count.
  - Carve differences are recorded as differences, not forced into one-to-one matches.
  - Translated terms stay flagged seeds.
  - Any quote that does not verify in the saved text fails that pass's build.
- **Jurisdiction splits:**
  - **Dutch:** Netherlands only. Flemish Belgium is a separate pair.
  - **Portuguese:** Portugal only. Brazil is a separate pair.
  - **Swedish:** Sweden only. Finland-Swedish is a separate pair.
  - **Chinese:** mainland Simplified only. Singapore and Taiwan are separate.
  - **English:** tests the Canadian-English register against US, UK, Ireland, New Zealand, Australia and Singapore instruments, since the register is Canadian English and the variants show where it carries a Canadian sense.
- **Known gaps:** Denmark, Italy and China have no instrument leads in the base, so each pass builds its own instrument list. The pair-level French gaps also stand: Belgium, Switzerland and Canada-Québec are separate pairs, still unrun.
- **Cost:** this is eleven Opus agents at once, plus the two still running.
- **Outputs and rows:** each writes only under its own `terminology-pass/<pair>/` folder and the retrieval log, and nothing goes to the database. I'll spot-check quotes and commit their outputs as they report.

The German pass is in and pushed to PR #213. Of its 90 recorded quotes, all appear in the saved text. In 6 rows the recorded phrase is not contained in the quote; for example, the phrase "Schrägrampen (geneigte Verkehrswege" includes an opening bracket the quote cuts off. I spot-checked three rows and did not check the other three.

- **Read in full:** the federal workplace rule ASR V3a.2 (edition August 2012, amended May 2025), the Bavarian building code article on accessibility, and the federal statute's definition of "barrierefrei". The Bavarian technical building rules were read in part. BAuA blocked the download, so it came through the Wayback route.
- **Not obtained:** the body of DIN 18040-1/-2, which is paywalled. The record therefore shows how German law adopts accessibility and treats workplaces, not DIN's technical content. The pass flags that a "searched-absent" cell means nothing while DIN 18040 can't be read, so coverage needs a column saying which layer was read.
- **Counts:** 60 register concepts, with 53 found and 7 searched-absent (shelter, lockers, volume, lighting levels, ratio, reverberation time, colour temperature). There are 90 reverse-harvest rows.
- **Where German carves the field differently:**
  - "Ramp gradient" covers two German objects. The workplace rule's "Schrägrampen" are outside the rule's DIN ramp, and slope splits into along-route and across-route.
  - The field is organised by performance criteria and a two-senses principle, which the English register has no axis for.
- **Aliases:** the base's parameter-level German aliases (Rampenneigung, Wendekreis, Bedienkraft, Flurbreite and others) occur zero times in what was read.
- **Method defects:**
  - The register has no rows for performance criteria, for how a requirement is determined, or for the people a rule names.
  - A coverage cell has no slot for the Land or the adopting instrument; Bavaria excludes every "R"-marked requirement of DIN 18040-2.
  - Substring checks of aliases are wrong both ways, because of German inflection and soft hyphens in the extracted text.

The Japanese pass and the eleven new ones are still running; I'll commit them as they report.

- **Not obtained:** JIS T 9251 (tactile indicators) and JIS Z 8210 (pictograms). The standards site returned a maintenance page, and nothing was reconstructed from memory.
- **Counts:** of 60 register concepts, 50 are found and 8 are found only by search with the page unread. Two are searched-absent (microwave height and colour temperature). There are 104 observations and 53 reverse-harvest rows.
- **Where Japanese carves the field differently:**
  - The statute's ostomy toilet appears in the design guidance under a different name. The register has no ostomy concept, and an English "faucet" seed would point at the wrong object.
  - Ramp landings are set by rise (a landing at every 75 cm of height), not by run length. Contrast is a difference in lightness, hue or saturation, not a light-reflectance value, and reverberation has no time quantity.
- **Method defects:**
  - The register's recurring statements are not atomic, so they inflate coverage.
  - A "found" cell needs a field for whether the concept is the same, narrower, wider or on a different axis.
  - The quote search tool can't search inside PDFs and misses text that crosses furigana markup.
  - One instrument spells the same word two ways, so exact-string attestation needs variant folding.

The pass also flagged two problems in `references/standards-registry.md`: a dead MLIT URL, and JIS T 9251 given as 2001 where the lead says 2014. I did not edit either.

**Repository size:** a 60 MB MLIT guidance PDF was already committed and pushed in an earlier commit. It is under GitHub's 100 MB file limit, but it is now in history and the repository's `.git` is 423 MB. Say if you want large retrieval files kept out in future. I haven't changed anything.

German, French and Japanese are done. The eleven other passes are still running.

message.content: do we not already have loads of term aliases etc in our database

content.text:
Yes, there are plenty, but most have not been checked against anything real. The base holds 2,382 aliases across 15 languages for 94 terms, and 88 of those terms have non-English aliases (re-derive with `select count(*) from term_aliases`).

- **Provenance:** about 1,163 are model-generated, 880 have no provenance recorded, 304 are curated English, and 15 are verified (Indonesian, outside P1-3). None of the P1-3 non-English aliases has been checked against a source.
- **What the pilots found:** the French pass reports that only 17 of the 169 French aliases occur in the two arrêtés it read in full, and some of those hits are in an unrelated sense. The German pass found that the parameter-level German aliases (Rampenneigung, Wendekreis, Bedienkraft, Flurbreite, Nachhallzeit, Farbtemperatur and others) occur zero times in what it read. Some held aliases are word-for-word translations of English that neither instrument uses ("seuil de niveau", "largeur de couloir").
- **Coverage is narrow:** the 94 terms came from the earlier edition's vocabulary, so aliases exist for those concepts only. The survey and B651 concepts (slip resistance, nosing, edge protection, drainage, bollards and the rest) have none, in any language.

So the existing aliases are a usable starting set of search seeds and nothing more. That is how E4 already treats them, so the passes used them as seeds and never as findings. The passes show where each language's actual instrument phrases differ from them. Those phrases are what can be promoted to attested aliases, once the tooling PR merges.

It is generated by `tools/names_table.py` from each pass's own records. The Swedish pass was stopped before it finished, so the Swedish column is only partial.

**Swedish pass stopped:** the Swedish agent was terminated by a platform safeguard flag on a message. The error said it "sometimes happens with safe, normal conversations". **What the table is**
- Rows are the register concepts and columns are language-and-jurisdiction pairs. A cell with no mark holds phrases the instrument itself uses, verbatim.
- A `[seed]` cell is a model-generated search seed, not a finding. `— absent` means the instrument was read and doesn't treat the concept. `— not-read` or `— not-obtainable` means that couldn't be said.
- It currently has 109 rows and 9 pair columns: Danish, German, Spanish, Finnish, French, Japanese, Dutch, Portuguese and Swedish. Norwegian, Korean, Italian, Chinese and the English-variants passes are still running and will appear when the table is regenerated.
- 57 rows have a verbatim name in at least 5 pairs. 46 rows have one in at most 2, mostly because the passes worded some concepts differently.
- It covers one pair per language. Belgium, Switzerland, Canada-Québec, Ireland and the other pairs are not in it yet.

The Finnish pass is done and pushed to PR #213. I confirmed by script that all 66 of its quotes appear in the saved Finnish text.

- **Read in full:** Government decree 241/2017 on accessibility, the safety-in-use decree 1007/2017, and the Ministry of the Environment's 2018 guide (the figures are images and were skipped). The decree is a Government decree, not a ministry decree as the brief said, and it isn't in `research_code_leads`.
- **Counts:** of 75 concepts (the 60 register items plus 15 B651 headings RHFAC doesn't name), 38 are found, 19 found in part and 18 searched-absent. There are 69 reverse-harvest rows.
- **Not read:** the sound-environment decree 796/2017, so reverberation time is unresolved. Neither the fire-safety decree 848/2017 nor the cited standards were attempted.
- **Where Finnish carves the field differently:**
  - A single word, "kulkuväylä", covers the approach, the interior route and the ramp. There is no corridor concept and no minimum interior route width.
  - A ramp's run is limited by the rise of a continuous ramp, not by its length. Climate enters the geometry too: an outdoor ramp may exceed 5 % only if covered or kept ice-free.
  - Contrast is "tummuus" (darkness), never quantified, and sits in the safety decree.
- **Method defects:**
  - Finnish inflection and compounding defeat plain substring matching in both directions. "tukikaide" misses "tukikaiteiden", and "käytävä" falsely hits "porraskäytävä". The held-alias hit count is unreliable either way.
  - The word-for-word seeds ("käytävän leveys", "pyörähdysympyrä") occur in none of the texts; the decree's own word for the turning space is "kääntymistila".

The names table is regenerated, still at nine pairs. Norwegian, Korean, Italian, Chinese and the English-variants passes are still running, and the Swedish restart is still open.

The Danish pass is done and pushed to PR #213. All 80 of its quotes appear in the saved text, checked by script. The names table now has 12 pair columns (124 concept rows); I have not checked that Norwegian, Korean, Italian and Chinese are among them or read any of their rows.

- **Read in full:** nine access-relevant chapters of the Danish Building Regulations (BR18) and three free official guidance documents. The paid technical layer, DS Håndbog 186 and DS/ISO 21542, is not obtainable.

- **Counts:** of 75 concepts, 38 are found, 14 found in part and 23 searched-absent. There are 69 reverse-harvest rows. Only 19 of the 156 held Danish aliases occur in the texts, several by accident.
- **Where Danish carves the field differently:**
  - The regulation's domain word is "Adgangsforhold" (access conditions), not "tilgængelighed". In the regulation "tilgængelig" means open to the public, so a search seeded on "tilgængelighed" would miss its own access chapter.
  - Landing intervals use two bases: every 12 m by length outdoors, and every 0.60 m of rise on shared routes. "Stigning" also means riser height, so the held alias "stigning" for ramp gradient is a sense error.
- **Method defects:**
  - The base holds no Danish leads or sources, so the instrument list was built from one URL in the standards registry and the portal's navigation.
  - An HTTP 200 can be an empty shell, and the fetch tool doesn't flag it.
  - The agent wrote its prior expectations into the search log after the retrievals, not before, and the log says so.

Still running: Norwegian, Italian, Korean(?), Chinese and the English-variants passes. The Swedish restart is still your call.

I'm not certain which of those are still running: Korean already appears in the table's earlier pair list, so check the table's header if you need the current set.

  - **Bbl:** all its accessibility-bearing parts, read in Dutch. That is chapter 4.1, the rules on fall barriers, level differences (stairs and ramps) and moving parts, reverberation (galm), usability (bruikbaarheid, 4.5), accessibility (toegankelijkheid, 4.6) and lighting. I also read their chapter 3 counterparts for existing buildings, the general rules of chapter 5, the escape-door, alarm and intercom articles, and Bijlage I divisions A and B. The rest of the decree (fire, structure, energy, chapter 7) was skipped after grep checks.
  - **Bouwbesluit 2012:** repealed; its last version ends 2023-12-31. I read only its ramp articles and chapter 4.4–4.7, to compare how the two decrees divide the field.

  |---|---|

I checked each against its article in the text: none falls outside the article it is credited to.
  
  **Two most surprising differences from English:**
  - **Accessibility is a zone, not a feature.** The "toegankelijkheidssector" is a defined part of the building, "zelfstandig bruikbaar" (independently usable) for "personen met een functiebeperking". Floor area, height and use class trigger it. Owner-built dwellings are exempt from the whole accessibility division.
  - **Doors and thresholds are not the objects regulated.** The width rule applies to the opening ("doorgang", with a defined "vrije breedte"), not the door. The threshold is a "hoogteverschil groter dan 0,02 m". "drempel" never occurs in the Bbl, though the ministry's own page uses it. Ramps are capped by a 1 m rise rather than a run length, with no intermediate landing.
  
  **Overlap with the Belgian-sourced terms (not edited):**
  - **TERM-090 (level difference):** minted from the Flemish "niveauverschil". The Dutch phrase in the Bbl is "hoogteverschil" (48 hits); "niveauverschil" appears only inside "lucht-geluidniveauverschil", an acoustics term.
  - **TERM-092 (intermediate landing):** no Bbl counterpart ("tussenbordes" and "rustbordes" both 0).
  
  **Method defects:**
  - NL needs the BWB XML route; there is no helper for it in the repo, and my converter (`tools/x2t.py`) is ad hoc.
  - The standards registry and lead 98 are each partly wrong about NEN 9120: dead URL and "free to download" on one side, "paywalled" on the other. I did not correct either.
  - The register is shaped around criteria, so near-duplicate rows share observations.
  - The quantity words in catalogue 2.2 match only in other senses, and I set those FOUND-PARTIAL by hand.
  - The register has no slot for trigger-based zoning, use-class switching or tenure exemptions, which is how the Dutch rule is built.

  - **NOT-OBTAINABLE:** GB 50763-2012 《无障碍设计规范》. The proxy refuses www.mohurd.gov.cn (CONNECT 502, logged), Wayback has no snapshot at the six addresses I tried (four of them my guesses), and only commercial copies turned up. content.text:
The Korean and Chinese passes are in and pushed to PR #213, and the names table is regenerated. All 69 Korean and 79 Chinese quotes appear in the saved text. For Chinese that check is against the agent's own transcription (below), so it proves less.

**Korean (South Korea)**
- **Read in full:** Enforcement Rule annex 1 (the detailed standards, already held as REF-01031, and current) and Enforcement Decree annex 2. The decree's mandatory/recommended matrix was read for structure only.
- **Counts:** of 75 concepts, 45 are found, 16 found in part and 14 searched-absent. There are 106 reverse-harvest phrases.
- **Turning space:** it is always a 1.4 m square or left unquantified, never a circle. One word, 활동공간, covers approach, transfer and landing space.
- **Operating force and reverberation:** neither appears. Doors are controlled by closing time and light material instead.
- **Ramps:** landings are spaced by rise, every 0.75 m, and ramp length appears only as the trigger for handrails.
- **Seeds:** every held Korean alias for the parameters is a word-for-word rendering found in no text. The instruments say 경사로의 기울기 for ramp gradient, 복도의 유효폭 for corridor width and 통과유효폭 for door clear width.
- **Not read:** the barrier-free certification criteria, any KS standard, and the transport act.

**Chinese (mainland, Simplified)**
- **Read in full:** GB 55019-2021, the fully mandatory code in force since 2022-04-01, and the 2023 Barrier-Free Environment Construction Law (arts. 1–72). The code's official PDF is scanned images, so the agent ran OCR and corrected every page against its image.
- **What the check proves:** quotes from the code are checked against that transcription, not against the PDF's own bytes. The law's quotes (16) do match the raw HTML. The agent caught and fixed one drift toward the expected word during transcription.
- **Not obtainable:** GB 50763-2012. The proxy refuses mohurd.gov.cn and Wayback holds no snapshot. A notice repeals only five of its mandatory clauses, so the rest still stands. Every "absent" result covers only two short texts and should be re-run once GB 50763 is obtained.
- **Counts:** 47 found, 17 found in part, 11 searched-absent. There are 95 reverse-harvest phrases.
- **Terms:** 扶手 means both handrail and door handle, so an English-led seed (把手) misses the code's word. One width word, 通行净宽, covers routes, ramps, doors and gates, and there is no corridor. A ramp run is limited by its rise, as in the Japanese pass.

The Chinese agent installed tesseract with apt in the container to get OCR. That is a container change, not a repository one.

Still running: Italian, Norwegian and the English-variants pass. The Swedish restart is still your call.

The Italian pass is in and pushed to PR #213, and the names table is regenerated. All 94 of its quotes appear in the saved text, checked by script.

- **Read in full:** DM 14 giugno 1989 n. 236 (arts 1–12) and DPR 24 luglio 1996 n. 503 (arts 1–31), from Normattiva.
- **Not read:** seven image-only graphic parts of the provisions (the manoeuvring-space, door-approach and control-height diagrams, the ramp graph and the art. 9 schemes). The original 1989 Gazzetta Ufficiale PDF is a scan and was not OCR'd. The law they implement was read only in part. Whether DM 236 is still current is unverified: one search reports a reform bill to repeal DM 236 and DPR 503, but no adopted replacement turned up.
- **Counts:** over the 60 register concepts, 39 are found, 15 found in part and 6 searched-absent (drainage, microwave, lockers, volume, reverberation time, colour temperature). There are 94 observations and 85 reverse-harvest rows.
- **Where Italian carves the field differently:**
  - Italian law grades the outcome in three defined levels: accessibilità, visitabilità and adattabilità. Adattabilità is "accessibilità differita"; visitabilità means access to the "spazi di relazione" plus one toilet. The register has no row for visitabilità.
  - The drafting has three layers (aims, prescribed specifications, and deemed-to-comply solutions) plus an equivalent-outcome route.
  - Operating force is "una pressione non superiore a 8 kg". Turning is a manoeuvre ("inversione di marcia", "spazi di manovra"), not a circle. Contrast, lighting and acoustics are never quantified, while slip resistance is a defined friction coefficient.
- **A transcription risk:** Normattiva's DM 236 at 4.1.9 reads "I corridoi devono presentare variazioni di livello", but the DM 236 reprint appended to DPR 503 reads "non devono". A transcription can drop a "non", so a second witness is needed for that clause.
- **Aliases:** only 7 of the 121 held Italian aliases occur in the texts. The parameter-level translations ("pendenza della rampa", "spazio di manovra", "forza di azionamento" and others) occur 0 times.

The agent installed tesseract with Italian in the container via apt and did not use it. Still running: the English-variants pass. The Swedish restart is still your call.

- **Other variants:** only the US says "elevator", and the UK uses "going" for a ramp flight's length as well as a step's tread depth.
- **Aliases:** 6 of the 13 jurisdiction-tagged English aliases in the base don't occur in their jurisdiction's text; "handicapped parking" is not in the ADA.

input.prompt:
You are the synthesiser for a wave of terminology research passes for the Accessible Built Environments Guidebook (/home/user/guidebook). Read CLAUDE.md first (rules 0, 5, 7a, 8, 10; sections 5 and 7). Then read in full: scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/terminology-pass/BRIEF.md; the four entries headed "Owner statements 2026-11-06" and the fifth in references/project-standards.md (the last entries of that file); scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/rhfac-b651-catalogue.md and base-population-plan.md (sections B and C); and EVERY pass-record.md under scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/terminology-pass/*/ (DA-DK, DE-DE, EN-VARIANTS, ES-ES, FI-FI, FR-FR, IT-IT, JA-JP, KO-KR, NL-NL, NO-NO, PT-PT, ZH-CN; SV-SE is being rerun and may be unfinished: use it only if it has a pass-record.md, and say which you used). Skim each pair's coverage.tsv and reverse-harvest.tsv where a claim needs checking. Do not modify any pass folder. Do not touch data/guidebook.db, commit or push.

Write ONE file: /home/user/guidebook/scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/terminology-pass/SYNTHESIS.md (at most 300 lines, tables where comparison is the point, Canadian English, objective tone, verdict first, no flattery, no recap). Contents, in this order:
1. **Verdict** in three sentences: what the wave established, what it did not, and the one change that most improves the next round.
2. **Method defects across passes**, de-duplicated and ranked by what wrong thing reaches the guidebook (CLAUDE.md section 5 failure modes), each with the passes that reported it, the count of passes (computed, not guessed), and the smallest fix under the owner's rule of 2026-11-06 to minimise code (try, in order: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code). Classify each fix as register change, protocol change, or tooling (tooling ships in its own PR, rule 10). Include the retrieval_log.locate_quote PDF/entity blindness, substring alias matching, text-match-not-sense-match, near-duplicate register rows inflating FOUND, retrieval of JavaScript shells with HTTP 200, the Wayback helper gap, scanned/OCR texts and the need to mark a transcription, priors written after the call, and anything else the records show.
3. **Register changes the carves demand.** The English register is object-shaped and Canadian. From the records, list the structural things non-English instruments organise the field by that the register has no slot for (examples reported: performance criteria and the two-senses principle in German; trigger-based zoning and use-class switching in Dutch; three defined outcome levels (accessibilità / visitabilità / adattabilità) in Italian; aim-then-prescription drafting and equivalent-effect routes in French and Italian; a cognitive-accessibility regime with its own frame in Spanish; climate in the geometry in Finnish; hazard and attention tactile fields in Norwegian; unit of limit (rise versus run) for ramps in Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Finnish, Norwegian, Dutch; the ostomy toilet; the word-for-word translation seeds that point at the wrong object). Group them: (a) new CONCEPTS for the register, (b) new KINDS of row (performance criterion, trigger, defined level, drafting layer), (c) SENSE SPLITS of an existing concept (ramp, level, washroom/lavatory, tread/going, corridor), (d) concepts English names that no instrument uses. For every item cite the pair(s) and the observed phrase(s), copied from the TSVs, not from memory.
4. **Coverage reality.** One table: pair, instruments read in full, instruments not obtainable, FOUND / FOUND-PARTIAL / ABSENT / reverse-harvest counts (computed with commands from the TSVs; note that pilots used 60 concepts and the later passes 75, and the EN pass 82), and the single largest unread layer for that pair (for example DIN 18040, NEN 9120, GB 50763, AS 1428.1, JIS, UNI, the regional codes). State plainly that 'absent' means absent from what was read.
5. **What may be promoted to the base, and how.** Using the base-population-plan's route (observe-term, adjudicate-term, add-term --from-observation or add-alias, which now attaches an observation pointer to a held alias): estimate by computation how many distinct verbatim phrases across all passes are candidate observations, how many would attest an existing held alias in place, how many would name a new concept, and how many are reverse-harvest concepts with no English term (E1: named by the instrument's own phrase). Do not propose any row; propose the order and the review unit (one instrument per review). Flag that every quote must verify and that three passes verified against a transcription or extracted text, not raw bytes.
6. **Decisions for the owner**, numbered, each a prompt with a recommended option first and the consequence of each option, phone-sized. Include at least: which pairs to run next (Belgium Dutch and French, Switzerland, Canada Québec, Ireland proper, the regional codes of Spain, Italy and Germany, Taiwan and Singapore Mandarin are not covered); whether to obtain the paid standards named above; whether the register is restructured before the next round or the next round runs on it unchanged; and the owner's licensing question about holding retrieved PDFs now settled by ruling.
7. **Self-attack**: the five likeliest ways this synthesis is wrong, each with how to detect it.

Every number is the command that derives it plus its result, dated 2026-11-06. Invent nothing; if a pass record does not say, write [GAP]. Reply to me in at most 10 lines: the verdict, the three highest-ranked defects, the number of register-change items by group, and the file path.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

The Swedish restart is done and pushed, so all 14 languages now have a pass. The names table is regenerated with 19 columns. All 104 of its recorded quotes appear in the saved text, checked by script.

**Swedish**
- **Instrument change:** the brief pointed at the building regulations (BBR), but Boverket's own page says BFS 2026:9 repealed them on 1 Oct 2026. The in-force texts are BFS 2024:12 (building accessibility), BFS 2024:9 (safety in use), BFS 2024:13 (plots), and the obstacle-removal rules (HIN). The repeal date rests on one Boverket web page; the text of BFS 2026:9 was not retrieved.
- **Audit of the cut-off files:** the restart agent re-read all four texts in full and discarded nothing. It corrected one line in the instruments table, where a chapter had been wrongly marked skipped. All 104 observation quotes and 100 reverse-harvest quotes verify, and the text files match `pdftotext` output of the persisted PDFs.
- **Not attempted:** the noise rules (BFS 2024:10), the dwellings rules (BFS 2024:11), the elevator standard SS-EN 81-70, and ALM 2. Amendment status of BFS 2024:12 and HIN is unverified, because Boverket's listing pages are JavaScript shells.
- **Counts:** 40 found, 20 found in part, 15 searched-absent. There are 100 reverse-harvest rows, and 39 observations come from HIN's non-binding advice text.
- **Where Swedish carves the field differently:**
  - The measures have left the binding rule. BFS 2024:12 fixes only a reference wheelchair footprint, a turning circle, a clear-passage opening, a 1:12 ramp and a lift size. Corridor width is "to be determined from layout and length", with no figure.
  - The two-group population ("nedsatt rörelse- eller orienteringsförmåga") puts hearing and cognition under "orientation". HIN gives contrast as NCS lightness contrast 0,40, not light-reflectance value.
- **Aliases:** all eight parameter-level Swedish translation aliases occur in none of the four instruments.

**Conflation:** your point that the literature conflates terms is recorded in the sixth ledger entry. Equivalence is judged per occurrence by the sense the source gives the form, and where a source conflates, the register records a conflation note with its locator and doesn't settle it by fiat. I've also told the synthesis agent to add a conflation sub-group drawn from the passes' own records, and it is still running.
